_note: Single source of truth for native test envs; run test/gen_test_envs.py to regenerate platformio.ini. A hardware path is host-testable: an env declares the capability it needs and the mocks under core_setup/hal/host stand in for silicon, including a queue keyed by handle. NEVER rewrite this file with json.dump: a whole-file re-render is valid JSON and reformats all 400 envs, so the diff stops naming what changed. Mutate it with harness.py env add/update/addsrc/remove, or from a script through harness.splice_replace + harness.write_verified, which refuses a write that moved an env it was not asked to move.

native_accept_gate.desc:
Accept-time connection gates with their flags ON (PROTOCORE_ENABLE_ACCEPT_THROTTLE
/ PER_IP_THROTTLE / IP_ALLOWLIST): the global fixed-window throttle, the per-source-IP
bucket table (independent budgets, window rollover, the millis() wrap, bounded LRU
eviction), and the CIDR source-IP allowlist. Compiles the flag-guarded accept-callback
paths that no other env builds. Budgets overridden small so the boundaries are explicit.

native_ad9238.desc:
AD9238 SPI configuration-port codec (server/peripherals/ad9238): the 16-bit instruction word
(R/W + byte-count + 13-bit address) for single-byte register writes/reads, the device-update
transfer transaction, and the input-validation fail-closed paths (null buffer, undersized
cap, zero/oversize byte count, out-of-range address). Pure host tests - the SPI clocking and
the per-register bit-field meanings are the datasheet's / the application's, not this codec's.

native_ads.desc:
Beckhoff ADS / AMS codec (services/fieldbus/ads): the AMS/TCP + AMS-header request builders
(little-endian, target-before-source addressing, cmd id + state flags + cbData + invoke id) for
Read/Write/ReadWrite/ReadState/ReadDeviceInfo/WriteControl/Add+DeleteNotification + the response
parsers incl. the DeviceNotification stamp/sample walk. TwinCAT PC-based control. Pure host tests.

native_ads1115.desc: ADS1115 16-bit ADC codec and its I2C binding (server/peripherals/ads1115): building the 16-bit config word for a single-shot single-ended reading (channel MUX, gain, data rate, start/mode/comparator bits, with out-of-range fallbacks), converting a signed 16-bit sample to microvolts across the gain's full-scale range, and reading a part end to end - the suite puts a voltage on a pin of the SBAS444E device model in core_setup/hal/host/devices/ and the driver's own transfers bring back the code the part computes for it.

native_amqp.desc:
AMQP 0-9-1 frame codec (services/iot/amqp): the protocol header, the frame + method
builders, the heartbeat, and the frame/method parsers (type/channel/size/payload/0xCE).
Pure host tests.

native_arena.desc:
Unified double-ended server arena (server/core/protocore_arena): first-fit
persistent end (bottom, individual free + coalesce + boundary shrink) + bump scratch end
(top, mark/release/reset) sharing a floating middle; fail-closed at the boundary. Host tests.

native_atc.desc:
ATC field-I/O interop snapshot (services/machine_tool/atc): serialize this device's field-I/O map
as {"inputs":[...],"outputs":[...]} JSON for an ATC engine over HTTP, plus the output setter and
value getter. Pure host tests.

native_audit_log.desc:
Tamper-evident hash-chained audit log (server/security/audit_log). Pure - the chain is
identical on host and ESP32 - so it unit-tests on the host; SHA-256 comes from
crypto/sha256 (software path on native), the timestamp from the pluggable clock.

native_auth_lockout.desc:
Per-IP brute-force auth lockout (server/security/auth_lockout): exponential-backoff
lockout state machine. Pure core (the millisecond clock is passed in), so it
unit-tests on the host. PROTOCORE_ENABLE_AUTH_LOCKOUT (and its required parent
PROTOCORE_ENABLE_AUTH) are set so the flag-guarded code compiles.

native_bacnet.desc:
BACnet/IP BVLC + NPDU codec (services/fieldbus/bacnet): the BVLC envelope (type 0x81,
function, length) + the NPDU header (version + NPCI control + optional DNET/DADR + hop
count) builders and parsers, slicing the APDU. ASHRAE 135. Pure host tests.

native_codec_base64.desc: The base64 codec (network_drivers/presentation/codec/base64) against RFC 4648: the seven sec 10 BASE64() vectors verbatim in both directions, the sec 4 Table 1 and sec 5 Table 2 spellings of alphabet values 62 and 63 (plus and slash against minus and underline), and the sec 3.3 requirement that encoded data holding characters outside the alphabet in use MUST be rejected, which each alphabet is checked against with the other's two characters as well as with a short quad, a pad before the tail and padding mid-stream. Also the destination-capacity guard on each of the three octets a quad writes, the unpadded final groups of sec 3.2 that base64url decodes, and a round-trip identity over every tail length in both alphabets, which checks the table-driven encoder against the branchless constant-time decoder rather than either against itself. This is the default SWAR decode path; native_codec_base64_scalar runs the same suite with PROTOCORE_BASE64_SWAR=0.

native_codec_base64_scalar.desc: The base64 scalar constant-time decode fallback (PROTOCORE_BASE64_SWAR=0): classify one character at a time instead of the default four-per-word SWAR path. Runs the same RFC 4648 suite as native_codec_base64, which proves the two decoders answer identically on the sec 10 vectors, on both sec 4 and sec 5 alphabets, on the sec 3.3 refusals, on the capacity guard and over the round-trip corpus.

native_bitio.desc:
The LSB-first bit writer (mmgr/bitio.h) the DEFLATE encoder and the SSH
zlib@openssh.com compressor both write their bitstreams through. Bits are read back by a bit
reader written in the test, so the packing order is asserted against a decoder's walk rather than
against the writer's own accumulator. Covers the whole-byte spill out of the accumulator, a
single put wider than a byte, the zero padding an align puts in the high bits of a partial byte,
an align on a boundary emitting nothing, and the capacity edge: an exact fill is not an overflow,
a byte past cap latches it and leaves the byte past cap untouched, and an align with no room
latches rather than writing.

native_mmgr_bitio.desc: LSB-first bit writer (mmgr/bitio.h) against RFC 1951: the sec 3.1.1 packing order, the sec 3.2.3 block header, the sec 3.2.6 fixed-Huffman end-of-block code (the empty final block is the octets 03 00), and the sec 3.2.4 stored-block LEN/NLEN pair. Plus the capacity edge: an exact fill is not an overflow, a spill past cap latches and stores nothing, an align with no room latches, and the flag never clears.

native_ble_gatt_att.desc: Bluetooth ATT codec and GATT characteristic bridge (services/radio/ble_gatt/ble_gatt.c): the Core Specification Vol 3 Part F section 3.4 PDU layouts and their section 3.4.8 opcodes with little-endian attribute handles, the section 3.4.1.1 Error Response, the Vol 3 Part G section 3.3.1.1 characteristic property bits, and the northbound RFC 8259 JSON view of a characteristic table. Pure host tests.

native_bus_capture.desc:
CAN listen-only capture framing (server/signaling/bus_capture): can_to_socketcan() building the
16-byte Linux SocketCAN frame (big-endian can_id, EFF/RTR flags, length, data) and the
DLT_CAN_SOCKETCAN libpcap link type. Pure host tests.

native_bus_wire.desc:
End to end from the host harness through the library: a real peripheral driver is called, it
goes through the real I2C / SPI bus owner, and the bytes it put on the wire are asserted. Covers
the SHT3x measurement command and its CRC-checked reply, the PCA9685 five-byte channel write,
the INA219 big-endian register order, the RTC register-pointer-then-burst read and its write,
SMBus with and without the PEC, the little-endian SMBus word, a full bus scan, and that a device
that does not acknowledge makes the driver report failure.

native_bytes.desc:
The byte verbs (mmgr/bytes.h): append into a protocore_span, take out of a protocore_cspan, and the
offset-passing reads a parser walks a raw payload with. The append side keeps counting pos past
cap on overflow, so an undersized region reports the capacity it should have had instead of only
failing - asserted on both the single byte and the multi-byte width. The take side is checked at
the boundary and one past it, with the sticky error and a refused read leaving both the cursor and
the output untouched. The length-prefixed blob reads are the peer-controlled path: the prefix is a
full u32 the peer picks, size_t is 32 bits on esp32 and c2000, and every bound here is a
subtraction against the space that remains rather than a sum that would wrap - a 0xFFFFFFFF prefix
is refused with the offset back where it started, and an exact fit is still accepted.

native_mmgr_bytes.desc: Byte verbs (mmgr/bytes.h) against RFC 4251 sec 5: the worked uint32 (0x29b7f4aa -> 29 b7 f4 aa), the worked string ("testing" -> 00 00 00 07 ...), and the mpint table, whose leading-zero rule mpint_fixed undoes. Plus the region contracts: a write past cap stores nothing and the cursor reports the capacity needed, a refused read leaves the cursor and the destination alone, and a peer-chosen full-range u32 length is refused on the space that remains rather than admitted by a sum that wrapped.

native_c37118.desc:
IEEE C37.118.2 synchrophasor frame codec (services/energy/c37118): CRC-CCITT, the frame
builder + Command frame, and the CRC-validating parser (type / ids / timestamp / payload).
Pure host tests.

native_canopen.desc:
CANopen (CiA 301) message codec (services/fieldbus/canopen): NMT, SYNC, heartbeat, EMCY,
PDO, and expedited SDO read/write/abort + the COB-ID classifier, over the shared CAN
frame (shared/can/can.h). Pure host tests.

native_codec_cbor.desc: The CBOR codec (network_drivers/presentation/codec/cbor) against RFC 8949. The load-bearing case transcribes Appendix A Table 6, which prints a diagnostic value beside its encoding in hex: each of the five head forms of sec 3 (immediate then 1, 2, 4 and 8 argument octets), both integer majors, byte and text strings including the multi-octet UTF-8 rows, nested arrays, maps, and the three simple values, all as the table's own octets rather than as whatever the encoder emits. Around it: the sec 3.3 float forms that this codec carries (0xfa single on the way out, single or double on the way in), the RFC 8428 Table 4 SenML label number the CBOR representation writes where JSON writes a string, head-form round trips at every argument width, overflow accounting that reports the capacity a payload needed, and the refusals: reserved and indefinite-length additional information (sec 3.2), tags (major 6), a declared string length past the end of the region, a truncated item, a type mismatch, and the sticky read error that stops a decoder resynchronizing by accident.

native_cc1101.desc:
CC1101 sub-GHz radio driver (services/radio/cc1101): the TI SPI header protocol (config
registers, command strobes, status registers, TX/RX FIFO) - init/detect, variable-length send, TX-done,
set-rx, packet recv with appended RSSI/LQI, and RSSI-to-dBm decode, against a mock chip. Host tests.

native_cclink.desc:
CC-Link cyclic fieldbus frame codec (services/fieldbus/cclink): the frame ([station][command][bit
data][word data][sum]) build + parse and the bit/word process-image accessors. Pure host tests.

native_cia402.desc:
CiA 402 / IEC 61800-7-201 drive profile (services/fieldbus/cia402): the Statusword power-state
decode (mask/value table), the Controlword commands + enable sequence, Statusword flags, the
CANopen SDO setters (Controlword / Modes / target position-velocity-torque) and cyclic PDO
pack/unpack. Layers on services/canopen. Pure host tests.

native_cip.desc:
CIP message codec (services/fieldbus/cip): the EPATH logical-segment builder, the request
builders (Get_Attribute_Single), and the response parser (service / status / data). Rides
an EtherNet/IP Unconnected Data item. Pure host tests.

native_client.desc:
Outbound TCP client transport (network_drivers/transport/tcp/tcp_client.c), the pooled
layer-4 peer of tcp.c used by http_client / mqtt / ws_client / relay / smtp / ssh
port-forward (PROTOCORE_NEED_CLIENT). The marshaled path is driven against the host pcb driver:
the connect completes inline, sends land in the capture, and received bytes arrive through
the recv callback the client armed. Covers the dial, the ring, the peer FIN and pool exhaustion.

native_clock.desc:
Pluggable monotonic clock (server/clock): default millis(), custom clock
divided down to the internal 1000 Hz, plus the microsecond base and latency
budgeting. Builds server/clock/clock.c, which owns the installed-clock state.

native_cloudevents.desc:
CloudEvents v1.0 envelope (services/iot/cloudevents): the structured-JSON builder
(over the JSON writer) + the binary-mode ce-* header reader. Pure host tests.

native_coap.desc:
CoAP server (RFC 7252) message codec + resource dispatch. Pure core - no
lwIP/UDP - so it unit-tests on the host (udp_transport provides host stubs).

native_coap_observe.desc:
CoAP with resource observation (RFC 7641) enabled. Compiles + runs test_coap
with PROTOCORE_ENABLE_COAP_OBSERVE on, so the Observe-gated code (request Observe
recording, the observer registry, protocore_coap_notify) is actually built in CI instead
of bit-rotting (it is enabled by no other env).

native_coaps.desc:
CoAP over DTLS (services/iot/coap/coaps, RFC 7252 sec 9): the bridge that drives a DtlsConn
handshake and, once established, unwraps each epoch-3 application record, answers it with
coap_server_process(), and re-wraps the response. An in-test DTLS 1.3 client completes the handshake
and exchanges a CoAP GET, decrypting the CoAP response from the returned DTLS record; a replayed
application record is dropped. Pure host tests.

native_coaps_server.desc:
CoAP-over-DTLS server front-end (services/iot/coap/coaps_server), the PROTOCORE_HAS_NET_STACK arm: the
per-peer DtlsConn pool + poll seam on top of protocore_coaps_process(), reached the way the target reaches it.
An in-test DTLS 1.3 client drives the server through the host UDP driver, which calls the recv callback the
core armed, and its replies are read out of that driver's send capture; each turn of the loop polls the
UdpListener then the server, in session.c's order. Exercises peer-address routing, the handshake + CoAP
exchange, the poll-driven retransmission timer (RFC 9147 sec 5.8), idle-connection reaping and a refused
send. Two simultaneous peers are routed to their own connections. The seam-only cases live in
native_coaps_server_nostack, which builds the other arm. Pure host tests.

native_coaps_server_nostack.desc:
CoAP-over-DTLS server front-end (services/iot/coap/coaps_server), the arm with no network stack: the
same suite, driven through the injection seam that arm has instead of a receive path.
coaps_server_ingest queues a datagram and an installed out-sink takes every reply, so ring_push's own
refusals - a zero-length datagram, an over-long one, an ingest ring already full, an address that will
not render - are read off the answer ingest reports, which udp_ingest_cb discards on the other arm.
PROTOCORE_HAS_NET_STACK is absent here because this env IS the other arm of it; native_coaps_server
builds the one where it is set. Pure host tests.

native_codeql.desc:
CodeQL coverage env: the full app compiled with every new feature flag ON so
CodeQL traces the integration paths (CSRF / lockout / allowlist gates,
permessage-deflate) AND the new service modules, which the per-feature envs scan
only in isolation. Built (--without-testing) by the CodeQL workflow; one test
in the filter is enough to pull in the whole src set.

native_compliance.desc:
RFC-compliance suite: builds with all enforcement at production defaults
(PROTOCORE_ENFORCE_HOST_HEADER=1) and exercises the strict behaviors.

native_concurrency.desc:
Concurrency proof for the cross-thread slot fields (protocore_atomic state / rx_head /
rx_tail). Two threads drive one slot's SPSC ring with the production access
pattern; asserts byte-exact in-order delivery. Portable (-pthread), runs on any
host including Windows - this verifies the data integrity / logic.

native_config_io.desc:
Schema-driven config export/restore (server/storage/config_io) over the config store;
round-trip host-tested against the in-memory backend.

native_config_store.desc:
Typed NVS config store (server/storage/config_store): string/u32/blob round-trips,
defaults, capacity, erase/clear - run against the host NVS backend that hal/nvs.h
selects off-target (the ESP32 Preferences backend is compiled in only on-target).

native_system_control.desc: PID control law (services/system/control): each term of the parallel form derived by hand from the difference equations control.h states (P, I accumulation, derivative-on-measurement with its low-pass, feed-forward), output clamping, anti-windup by conditional integration freezing and releasing the accumulator, the hard integral clamp, the fixed-rate entry point against the variable-rate one, the batched multi-axis pass, the inline clamp/deadband/slew/low-pass primitives, and the dense-binary PID log header and record layouts. No standard publishes PID vectors; expectations are properties plus documented arithmetic.

native_cotp.desc:
TPKT (RFC 1006) + COTP X.224 class-0 frame codec (services/fieldbus/cotp): the TPKT
envelope, the COTP Data TPDU + Connection Request builders, and the COTP parser. The
ISO-on-TCP foundation under S7comm / IEC 61850 MMS. Pure host tests.

native_wycheproof_kat.desc: Data-driven external known-answer tests for the shared crypto primitives: HMAC-SHA256/512, AEAD_AES_128_GCM (crypto/aead/aes128gcm.h), X25519, Ed25519 verify and sign, HKDF-SHA256 Extract and Expand, the ChaCha20 block and Poly1305. Vectors come from kat_data.inc - Project Wycheproof at a pinned commit plus RFC 5869 Appendix A and RFC 8439 sections 2.4.2 and 2.5.2 - so the adversarial rows (flipped tag bit, truncated tag, low-order point, malleable S) are exercised as well as the well-formed ones. Adds the RFC 5869 sec 2.3 length cap and the GCTR counter carry past 256 blocks.

native_x509.desc: RFC 5280 certificate parsing and RFC 6125 name matching (crypto/x509). Checked against real certificates OpenSSL made - an Ed25519 CA with basicConstraints/keyUsage, and Ed25519, P-256 and RSA leaves under it - and against the values OpenSSL reports for them, so a field read wrong is a disagreement with an independent encoder rather than with the author. The name-matching cases are sec 6.4.3's three wildcard rules and each way a wildcard can be stretched past them: spanning a dot, matching the bare domain, and a certificate with no SAN matching nothing at all (sec 6.4.4 forbids the common-name fallback).

native_x509_verify.desc: RFC 5280 sec 6.1 path validation (crypto/x509_verify): one link checked four ways - the signature over the TBS under the issuer's key, the validity window, whether the issuer may sign at that depth, and the issuer-name match. Driven with the same OpenSSL-made certificates test_x509 parses, one CA per algorithm so the Ed25519, P-256 and RSA verification paths are each reached by a certificate an independent implementation signed.

native_wycheproof_kat_hw.desc: The crypto KATs a second time with the accelerator arms selected, answered by the host HALs so both arms run natively.

native_csrf.desc:
Stateless HMAC-signed CSRF token (server/security/csrf): issue/verify with a fixed
secret unit-tests on the host (PROTOCORE_ENABLE_CSRF set). Pulls in the SSH
HMAC-SHA256 + SHA-256 core.

native_ct_eq.desc:
protocore_ct_eq (crypto/ct_eq.h): the one comparator every AEAD tag, MAC, digest and
signature check goes through. Equal buffers, a difference at every byte position, single-bit
differences, zero length, and that it reads exactly n bytes and no more.

native_ct_eq_unit.desc: The library's one secret-dependent comparator (crypto/ct_eq.h). No standard publishes a vector for a compare and the timing claim needs a cycle counter on the die, so every case is a property: the differing octet swept across every position at every length, single-bit differences, the walk stopping exactly at n, OR-accumulated differences that must not cancel, symmetry, and the high bit surviving the accumulate.

native_dbm.desc:
Log-structured hash key-value store on the WAL (services/storage/dbm): put/get/delete with an
in-RAM open-addressed index and value data appended to the write-ahead log, plus index rebuild by
replaying the log on open. Pure host tests over a RAM-backed WalDev, incl. overwrite, tombstone
resurrection, persistence across a remount (with and without checkpoint), collisions, index-full
fail-closed, key/value bounds, and a max-size value round-trip.

native_dds_rtps.desc: DDSI-RTPS Message framing codec (services/iot/dds), OMG DDSI-RTPS 2.5 formal/2022-04-01: the sec 9.4.4 20-octet Header (PROTOCOL_RTPS magic, ProtocolVersion, VendorId, GuidPrefix), the sec 9.4.5.1 SubmessageHeader with octetsToNextHeader in the byte order the EndiannessFlag names, the sec 9.4.5.1.1 SubmessageKind octets, the sec 9.4.5.1 octetsToNextHeader==0 rule and its PAD / INFO_TS exception, and the sec 8.3.6.3 / sec 8.3.4.1 Header and Submessage validity refusals. Pure host tests.

native_der.desc: ASN.1 DER reader (shared/der): the X.690 canonical subset X.509 is parsed with. The accepting cases are RFC 5280 sec 4.1's Certificate SEQUENCE and the sec 4.1.2.5 times; the refusing ones are each a BER spelling DER forbids - indefinite length (sec 8.1.3.6), a long form that fits the short one or carries a leading zero (sec 10.1), a redundant leading zero on an INTEGER (sec 8.3.2), a negative INTEGER read as unsigned (sec 8.3.3), a BIT STRING with unused bits (sec 8.6.2.2), and a multi-octet tag (sec 8.1.2.4). Accepting a second encoding of a certificate is accepting one the signature does not cover.

native_codec_deflate.desc: The RFC 1951 DEFLATE compressor (network_drivers/presentation/codec/deflate), the WebSocket permessage-deflate sender. The load-bearing case derives the exact output octets for three inputs from RFC 1951 alone - sec 3.2.3's block header, sec 3.2.6's fixed code table, sec 3.2.5's length and distance codes, sec 3.1.1's bit order and RFC 7692 sec 7.2.1's stripped 00 00 ff ff tail - with the bit-by-bit derivation written beside the bytes, so a compressor that agreed with its own decompressor while emitting a non-conforming stream fails here rather than passing. The rest is round-trip identity through INFLATE over text, the empty input, a single octet, every octet value, highly repetitive input that must actually shrink, a chain walk driven past its budget, a candidate match past the window that must be discarded, and random and low-entropy corpora; plus the fail-closed paths for an output buffer and a scratch buffer that are too small.

native_device_id.desc:
MAC-derived device UUID (server/signaling/device_id): RFC 4122 v5 from a MAC via SHA-1.
Pure core - the ESP32 MAC read is ARDUINO-gated - so it unit-tests on the host
against Python uuid.uuid5 reference values.

native_devicenet.desc:
DeviceNet link-adaptation codec (services/fieldbus/devicenet): the 4-group 11-bit CAN id,
explicit-message header octet, single-frame explicit messages, and the fragmentation
reassembler (CIP over CAN; the CIP body is built with the cip codec). Pure host tests.

native_df1.desc:
Allen-Bradley DF1 full-duplex frame codec (services/fieldbus/df1): BCC + CRC-16/ARC, the
frame builder with DLE byte-stuffing, and the validating, un-stuffing parser. Vectors from
AB pub. 1770-6.5.16. Pure host tests.

native_diag.desc:
Build-flag reporter (diag() / PROTOCORE_ENABLE_DIAG). The gated diag() entry point
and its DIAG_DOC frame spec are enabled by no other env, so this one keeps them
compiled + exercised in CI. Reuses the full app src via the native_stack_http
base.

native_diffserv.desc:
DiffServ QoS marking (PROTOCORE_ENABLE_DIFFSERV): the DSCP->TOS encode (DSCP << 2, ECN 0), the
server-wide and UDP DSCP defaults through the DiffServ entries and through the flat readers the
accept path uses, and the per-listener override (TcpListener.set_dscp, which names the port, incl.
the UNSET sentinel + 6-bit mask + unknown-port miss). A live connection has no setter: RFC 9293 sec
3.9.2 SHLD-23. The accept callback's three arms - per-listener override, server default, best-effort
skip - and a dynamic (forwarded) listener taking the sentinel. Pure L4 core, host-tested.

native_sha256_kat.desc: SHA-256 (crypto/hash/sha256.h) against the RFC 6234 sec 8.5 SHA256 known-answer vectors: 'abc', the 56-octet message whose padding overflows into a second block, one million 'a' fed as a stream, and a 640-octet message that is an exact multiple of the 512-bit block. The empty-message digest is the Transcript-Hash('') RFC 8448 sec 3 prints for the TLS 1.3 'tls13 derived' step. Adds chunk-split invariance, the header's contract that final() leaves the context running, and the one-shot / streaming equivalence.

native_aes_block.desc: The software AES block every software AES mode in the library sits on.

native_sha256_kat_hw.desc: The RFC 6234 SHA-256 vectors a second time with the accelerator arm selected, answered by the host SHA HAL so both arms run natively.

native_directnet.desc:
AutomationDirect DirectNET serial frame codec (services/fieldbus/directnet): the header (SOH +
ASCII-hex slave/type/addr/blocks + ETB + LRC) and data (STX + data + ETX + LRC) frames build/parse.
Pure host tests.

native_dma.desc:
DMA peripheral ingest / egress simulator (mmgr/dma), v5 hardware ingest: an
ingress feed surfaces as RX completion events, a full buffer ping-pongs and re-arms,
egress DMA is captured, TX is one-in-flight fail-closed, and a loopback channel
round-trips its own TX into RX. The preempt-queue hand-off is observable on the host
through the keyed queue mock; only the interrupt that triggers it needs hardware.

native_dmx.desc:
DMX512 + RDM lighting codec (server/peripherals/dmx): the DMX512 slot packet (build/get) and the
RDM (ANSI E1.20) packet build/parse with 48-bit UIDs and the 16-bit additive checksum. Pure
host tests.

native_dnc.desc:
CNC DNC drip-feed (services/machine_tool/dnc): the EIA RS-244 <-> ISO/ASCII tape-code translation
(odd-parity EIA table), ISO even parity, G-code block framing with '%' rewind-stop and leader
runout, XON/XOFF flow-control state, a streaming block reassembling decoder, and the dnc_stream
drip-feed engine (leader / markers / blocks over a send/recv seam, paced on reverse-channel
XON/XOFF). Pure host tests, incl. an odd-parity + exact-inverse table guardrail, full encode ->
decode program round-trips for both tape codes, and a scripted mock controller that decodes the
streamed program back and exercises the XOFF/XON pause-resume path.

native_dnp3.desc:
DNP3 (IEEE 1815) data-link frame codec (services/energy/dnp3): CRC-16/DNP, the frame
builder (0x0564 header + CRC'd 16-octet data blocks) and the CRC-validating, de-blocking
parser. Pure host tests.

native_dns_resolver.desc:
The portable DNS resolver (network_drivers/network/dns/dns_resolver, RFC 1035) on the build
where PROTOCORE_HAS_VENDOR_DNS_RESOLVER is 0: the A-record question it writes, the answer it reads back -
walking past a CNAME and following the compression pointers a real response uses - and the replies it
refuses on a wrong id, a set RCODE, a question rather than an answer, or no A record at all. Plus the
dotted-quad fast path, the nameserver setter, and the classifier that rejects a loopback or multicast
answer as a rebinding indicator.

native_dns_server.desc:
Authoritative DNS server (network_drivers/network/dns/dns_server): the A-record response builder
(QNAME parse, compressed A answer, NXDOMAIN, non-A query, header flags, malformed
guards), the built-in name->IP table (add / case-insensitive lookup / clear), and begin() binding
port 53 on the UDP listener, driven against the host pcb driver.

native_dns_wire.desc:
The DNS name on the wire (network_drivers/network/dns/dns_wire, RFC 1035 sec 3.1 / 4.1.4):
labels to a dotted string and back, compression pointers followed for an answer and refused for a
question, the hop limit that makes a self-referential message terminate, the undefined label types,
the label and destination bounds, and the case-insensitive compare names are defined to use.

native_dns_wire_codec.desc: DNS name codec (network_drivers/network/dns/dns_wire, RFC 1035). Rebuilds the worked message of sec 4.1.4 octet for octet at the offsets that figure names (F.ISI.ARPA at 20, FOO.F.ISI.ARPA at 40 ending in a pointer, ARPA at 64 as a bare pointer into the middle of the first name, the root at 92), and covers the sec 3.1 label encoding, the sec 2.3.4 63-octet label limit, the sec 4.1.4 reserved 10 and 01 label types, pointer-loop termination, output-buffer refusals, and the sec 2.3.3 case-insensitive comparison.

native_docstore.desc:
Local JSON document store on the WAL (services/storage/docstore): JSON documents addressed by id,
stored via dbm on the write-ahead log, plus top-level field queries (find documents whose JSON field
equals a value) via the zero-heap JSON reader. Pure host tests over a RAM-backed WalDev, incl.
put/get/delete, string/int/bool field finds, persistence + query across a remount, and early stop.

native_dshot.desc:
DShot ESC throttle codec (server/peripherals/dshot): the 16-bit frame (11-bit value + telemetry +
4-bit nibble-xor CRC), the bidirectional inverted-CRC variant, decode/validate, and per-rate bit
timing. Pure host tests with hand-computed vectors.

native_dtls.desc:
DTLS 1.3 record layer (network_drivers/presentation/security/dtls/dtls_record, RFC 9147 sec 4):
DTLSPlaintext + DTLSCiphertext protect/unprotect, the unified header, sequence-number encryption
(sec 4.2.3) and reconstruction (sec 4.2.2), the AEAD nonce, and the anti-replay window (sec 4.5.1).
The key + record KAT is byte-exact against an independent HKDF-Expand-Label + AEAD_AES_128_GCM +
AES-ECB reconstruction (RFC 5869 / RFC 8446 / SP 800-38D). Pure host tests.

native_dtls_conn.desc:
DTLS 1.3 server handshake state machine (network_drivers/presentation/security/dtls/dtls_conn,
RFC 9147 sec 5-6): the one-round-trip full handshake (TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 / X25519 / Ed25519)
over the DTLS record + framing layers, reusing the TLS 1.3 messages + key schedule. A minimal
in-test DTLS client completes the handshake end to end - deprotecting the server flight, verifying
the CertificateVerify signature and Finished MAC over the real transcript, and confirming both
sides install identical application-traffic keys. Also drives the HelloRetryRequest group
renegotiation (sec 5.1): a ClientHello with no X25519 key_share draws an HRR + address-bound cookie,
and the retry that echoes it completes over the message_hash || HRR || ClientHello2 transcript; a
retry without the cookie is rejected. An RFC 7250 Raw Public Keys case (PROTOCORE_ENABLE_TLS_RPK) offers
server_certificate_type = RawPublicKey and confirms the server answers with a 44-byte Ed25519
SubjectPublicKeyInfo whose key CertificateVerify signs. Pure host tests.

native_dtls_hs.desc:
DTLS 1.3 handshake framing + reliability (network_drivers/presentation/security/dtls/dtls_handshake,
RFC 9147 sec 5 + 7): the 12-byte DTLS handshake header, overlap-tolerant message reassembly, the
ACK message (content type 26), and the stateless HelloRetryRequest cookie (sec 5.1). The cookie
wire format is byte-exact against an independent Python-stdlib HMAC-SHA256, proving the field
layout and the client-address binding. Pure host tests.

native_dtls_tls13_rfc.desc: The TLS 1.3 messages the DTLS 1.3 handshake adds to tls13_msg, compiled for the DTLS path: the RFC 8446 sec 4.1.3 HelloRetryRequest random published as 32 hex octets, the sec 4.1.4 HelloRetryRequest built byte-exact for both the DTLS 1.3 (RFC 9147 sec 5.3) and TLS 1.3 version codepoints, the sec 4.4.1 message_hash transcript wrapper, the empty sec 4.3.1 EncryptedExtensions, the RFC 7250 negotiated server_certificate_type, the RFC 8410 sec 10.1 published Ed25519 SubjectPublicKeyInfo, the RFC 7250 RawPublicKey Certificate message, and the DTLS ClientHello parse of the cookie, server_certificate_type and RFC 9146 connection_id extensions plus the sec 5.3 empty-legacy_cookie rule.

native_edge_cache.desc:
CDN edge-cache engine (server/web/edge_cache): the pure freshness/validator core (response
header-field access, HTTP-date parsing over IMF-fixdate / RFC 850 / asctime, RFC 9111 lifetime +
Expires-Date + heuristic + corrected age, the canonical cache key + SHA-256 digest + Vary secondary
key, and the L1 LRU/TTL store + storeability rules), plus the async origin-fetch engine (completion
detection over Content-Length / chunked / connection-close, and the state machine over a mock transport
seam), plus the shared single-range `Range: bytes=...` parser (http_parse_byte_range) that backs serving
206 Partial Content windows from a cached body. Pure host tests.

native_edge_cache_core.desc:
CDN edge-cache pure engine (server/web/edge_cache/edge_cache) plus the shared single-range
`Range: bytes=...` parser it serves 206 windows with (network_drivers/application/http_range):
the RFC 9110 sec 5.6.7 three HTTP-date spellings of one instant, sec 5.1 / 5.5 response
field-value access, the sec 14.1.1 / 14.1.2 published byte-range examples and unsatisfiable
forms, RFC 9111 sec 4.2.1 freshness-lifetime precedence, sec 4.2.2 heuristic, sec 4.2.3
corrected initial age and current age, sec 4.1 Vary secondary key, sec 3 storeability, and
sec 4.3 conditional revalidation plus 304 freshening over the L1 LRU store. Pure host tests.

native_edge_cache_sd.desc:
CDN edge-cache L2 SD-persistence tier (server/web/edge_cache/edge_cache_sd): the entry <->
dbm-value serialization roundtrip (all response metadata, Vary variants, binary and max-size bodies),
the spill/promote/del/purge API over a dbm on a RAM-backed WalDev, the L1 store's on_evict write-back
hook, the storeability gates (no-validator and oversize entries stay L1-only), reboot survival via
remount + index replay, and that a shared dbm's foreign values are never touched. PROTOCORE_DBM_VAL_MAX is
sized below a full entry so the oversize-stays-L1 path is exercised. Pure host tests.

native_edge_mesh.desc:
CDN edge-cache mesh sibling-cache codec (server/web/edge_cache/edge_mesh): the request/response
wire frames (build + tri-state accumulating parse over partial reads, magic/version/opcode validation),
the freshness-carrying entry frame (the shared edge_sd body plus a timing trailer) round-tripped
byte-exact, RFC 9111 age propagation (a peer's corrected age transfers so the receiver stays fresh for
the remaining lifetime and its Age keeps growing), and the async peer-query engine reaching HIT / MISS /
FAILED (timeout, peer close, malformed) over a scripted mock transport seam. Pure host tests.

native_endian.desc:
The fixed-width serializers (mmgr/endian.h): a width moved between an integer and
the bytes at a pointer, both orders, 16/32/64. Each writer is diffed against a shift loop written
in the test rather than against its opposite number, so a pair that is wrong the same way both
ways cannot agree its way to a pass. Covers the returned width a caller advances by, the reader
inverting the writer, a big-endian encoding being the byte reverse of the little-endian one, the
round trip at every offset within a word (the file writes a byte at a time so a strict-alignment
die is served), and a narrow write leaving the bytes above it alone so packed fields do not
clobber each other.

native_mmgr_endian.desc: Fixed-width serializers (mmgr/endian.h) against RFC 1071 sec 3, whose numerical example prints one octet string and states each of its 16- and 32-bit fields in Normal (network) and Swapped order - the big- and little-endian readings published as numbers. RFC 4251 sec 5 supplies the writer side (699921578 stored as 29 b7 f4 aa) and the uint64 rule. Plus: writers return their width, touch only their width, round-trip at every offset in a word, and the two orders are byte reversals of each other.

native_enip.desc:
EtherNet/IP encapsulation codec (services/fieldbus/enip): the 24-octet header, RegisterSession
+ SendRRData builders (Common Packet Format), and the SendRRData reply extractor. Constants
per the Wireshark ENIP dissector. Pure host tests.

native_enocean.desc:
EnOcean ESP3 serial codec (services/radio/enocean), v5 radio plugin: the CRC-8 (poly 0x07)
against known answers, a build -> parse round trip, malformed framing (bad sync / header
CRC / data CRC), incomplete telegrams, over-length rejection, and resynchronisation.
Pure host tests.

native_enocean_esp3.desc: EnOcean ESP3 serial codec (services/radio/enocean/enocean.c): the CRC-8 the ESP3 specification section 3.3 defines (generator x^8+x^2+x^1+x^0, the catalogue's CRC-8/SMBUS) checked against the table that specification prints and against the catalogue check value, the section 1.7 telegram field layout with CRC8H over the header and CRC8D over the data and optional data, resynchronization on a bad sync or CRC, and the ERP1 radio telegram layout of RORG, payload, big-endian sender id and status. Pure host tests.

native_system_esp.desc: ESP packet transform with AES-256-GCM (services/system/esp): the RFC 4303 sec 2 wire layout read field by field off the packet (SPI and Sequence Number in network byte order, the RFC 4106 explicit IV in the clear, the ICV on a 4-byte boundary), the sec 2.4 right-alignment rule and the monotonic 1,2,3 padding it prescribes, SPI/Seq/Next-Header round trips, single-bit authentication of every octet, wrong-key and wrong-salt rejection, header-as-AAD, and the sec 3.4.3 anti-replay window (sequence 0 refused, duplicates, reordering inside the window, the 64-packet width, clean advance).

native_espnow_envelope.desc: ESP-NOW typed envelope and peer registry (services/radio/espnow/espnow.c): the magic/type/length header, exact-length and magic validation on decode, the payload cap derived from Espressif's published 250-octet ESP-NOW v1 data limit less the header, and the bounded no-heap peer registry. The envelope is not a standardized format, so the expectations are properties. Pure host tests.

native_euromap77.desc:
EUROMAP 77 (OPC 40077) IMM_MES_Interface model (services/machine_tool/euromap77) - OPC UA for injection
molding machines. The Browse hierarchy + the Read resolver over a bound EmImm, including the
UInt64 production counters, are host-tested here against the published NodeSet. The suite includes
euromap77.c so the Read and Browse resolvers are reachable - they answer the OPC UA server's handler
contract rather than this module's API - which is why the env does not build that .c itself.
Requires the OPC UA codec. No heap, no stdlib.

native_exc_decoder.desc:
ESP32 panic / exception decoder (server/exc_decoder): parse a captured Guru Meditation
dump (cause, register PC + EXCVADDR, backtrace PC:SP frames) into a structured ExcInfo and serialize it
as JSON for a live /exception panel; tolerates missing fields + a trailing corruption marker. Pure host tests.

native_failsafe.desc:
Software watchdog / deadlock detection + safe-state (server/failsafe): the wrap-safe
overdue predicate, the lifeline registry, fire-once-per-episode breach callback, and JSON.
Pure host tests with a synthetic clock.

native_fanuc_j519.desc:
FANUC Stream Motion / option J519 UDP codec (services/machine_tool/fanuc_j519): the robot
counterpart to FOCAS. The 8-octet little-endian header, all six packets (Start/Motion/Stop/Request
PC->robot, Robot Status/Ack robot->PC), the 9-axis IEEE-754 binary32 pose/joint/current blocks, and
the 20-entry threshold tables - byte-checked at every field offset against the public Wireshark
dissector, plus symmetric build->parse round trips. Includes the length guards that separate the two
packets sharing a type code per direction (Start 8 vs Status 132, Request 16 vs Ack 184). No heap,
no stdlib. Pure host tests.

native_fdc2214.desc:
FDC2114/2214 capacitance-to-digital field sensor (server/peripherals/fdc2214): the 28-bit data
combine + error flags, the frequency scale (data/2^28 * fref), and the single-channel config-sequence
builder. Pure codec host tests (the I2C binding is ESP32-only).

native_fins.desc:
Omron FINS frame codec (services/fieldbus/fins): the command builder + Memory Area Read
convenience + the command / response parsers (10-octet header, MRC/SRC, MRES/SRES end
code). Pure host tests.

native_float_bits.desc:
A double read as the three fields it is (mmgr/float_bits.h): sign at bit 63,
exponent at 62..52, mantissa at 51..0, by mask and shift, and merged back from those three. The
oracle is the layout written out in the test, not a second accessor. Covers that the three masks
partition all 64 bits exactly once, the known encodings (1.0 is the bias with a zero mantissa,
3.14159 is exponent 1024, negative zero differs from zero in the sign alone), the non-finite and
subnormal exponent fields, and the round trip: split into fields and merged back is the value that
went in, at every one of the 64 bit positions, so no field is a bit short or a bit wide. The merge
masks each field to its own width, so a field carrying junk above it cannot reach a neighbour.

native_mmgr_float_bits.desc: binary64 field reads (mmgr/float_bits.h) against IEEE 754 sec 3.4: the 1/11/52 interchange layout and bias 1023, with every expected word derived from that definition in the comment beside it (1.0 is 2^0, so its exponent field is 0 + 1023 -> 0x3FF0000000000000). Covers the two zeros, infinity and NaN sharing the all-ones exponent, the subnormal boundary, the largest finite value, per-field masking in the merge, and exhaustive round trips over all 64 bit positions and the whole exponent range.

native_flow_export.desc:
Flow-record export codec (services/net/flow_export): NetFlow v5 fixed header/record
builders + the NetFlow v9 / IPFIX template-then-data cursor (length/count patching,
v9 4-octet padding). Pure host tests with wire-byte assertions.

native_focas.desc:
FANUC FOCAS Ethernet codec (services/machine_tool/focas): the big-endian frame envelope
(magic/version/type/length) + open/close handshake, the generic command request (6-octet function
selector + five i32 args), and the response parsers (echoed selector + FOCAS return code + data),
incl. ODBSYS SysInfo, the alarm bitmask, and the 8-octet data/base^exp value encoding. FANUC CNC
data over TCP 8193, reverse-engineered vs diohpix/pyfanuc. Pure host tests.

native_forward.desc:
Interface forwarding plane (network_drivers/network/forward), v5 bridge / router: default-deny,
an ALLOW rule forwards, a DENY wins, multi-destination fan-out, no reflection to the
source, the per-rule rate cap (host test clock), send-failure counting, the interface /
rule table limits, the ingress ACL (byte-pattern permit/deny, first-match, default
action), policy routing (byte-pattern -> egress, precedence + fail-closed), and the opt-in
inspection hook. Pure host tests; the DMA-driven wiring is covered by native_dma over the same host queue.

native_forwarded_trust.desc:
Trusted-reverse-proxy forwarded-client resolver (server/security/forwarded_trust): a
Forwarded / X-Forwarded-For client address is honored only when the real TCP peer
is a configured trusted-upstream CIDR, else the TCP peer is kept. Pure (no
sockets), so it host-tests; a direct/untrusted peer's spoofed header is never
believed. PROTOCORE_ENABLE_FORWARDED_TRUST (+ its required parents AUTH / AUTH_LOCKOUT)
are set so the flag-guarded config compiles.

native_frame.desc:
The declarative frame builder (mmgr/protoframe.h + protoframe.c): the single engine that
turns a static protocore_field spec into wire bytes, so the ~160 formatting sites in this library carry
a table rather than a hand-written append sequence. Covers every field kind and width, the
fail-closed contract at the exact byte boundary (a frame that does not fit reports 0 AND leaves a
valid empty string, which is what a length comparison against snprintf's would-be length silently
got wrong), the append rewind that keeps a header line whole-or-absent, NULL string handling, and
a differential check of the numeric and float conversions against the libc printf whose output
these frames replace byte for byte.

native_mmgr_frame.desc: Declarative frame builder (mmgr/protoframe.h): every field kind rendered as the ISO C11 sec 7.21.6.1 conversion it names, widths that pad but never truncate, and the argument check that compares each value's kind and the arity against the spec. The load-bearing case is the fail-closed contract: a frame that does not fit returns 0 and writes an empty string, and the append form rewinds the whole frame, so a caller that ignores the return sends nothing rather than half a header line.

native_ftp.desc:
FTP client wire codec (services/file_transfer/ftp, RFC 959 + RFC 2428): the control-command
builders (generic verb + PORT + EPRT), the single/multi-line 3-digit reply parser, and the
PASV / EPSV data-address decoders. Pure host tests with authentic reply strings captured from a
live FTP server (multiline greeting + FEAT, PASV/EPSV tuples).

native_ftp_session.desc: The FTP client session (services/file_transfer/ftp/ftp_session.c): the stepped store over a real TCP client. RFC 959 sec 5.4's minimum command sequence for a STOR, with the RFC 2428 sec 3 EPSV reply and the RFC 959 sec 4.1.2 PASV fallback under it. Nothing in the matrix compiled this file before.

native_gateway.desc:
Radio / wireless gateway bridge (server/net/gateway), v5 southbound-to-northbound: an
uplink envelopes a received frame (src address / port / rssi / seq) and publishes it,
fail-closed on no sink / unknown port / rate cap / sink refusal; a downlink routes to the
port transmit callback; the topic helper formats <prefix>/<port>/<addr>; port table limits.
Pure host tests; the DMA + FORWARD-lane ingest is covered by native_dma and native_forward.

native_gnss_survey.desc:
GNSS survey-in core (services/timing_position/gnss/gnss_survey): the exact WGS84 geodetic<->ECEF
transform (matched against pyproj EPSG:4979->EPSG:4978), the shifted-origin position averager with a
3-D accuracy estimate, and the GGA->geodetic fold. Pure host tests.

native_gnss_survey_in.desc: GNSS survey-in core (services/timing_position/gnss/gnss_survey, suite beside the NMEA sentence codec it folds fixes from): the geodetic-to-ECEF transform reduced at the equator and the pole to WGS84's published semi-major axis 6378137.0 and semi-minor axis 6356752.3142, height along the ellipsoid normal, rotational and hemispheric symmetry, the iterative inverse round-tripped to sub-millimetre, RTCM 0.1 mm rounding half away from zero, the shifted-origin mean and population spread at ECEF magnitude, the observation/accuracy completion gate, and the GGA fold with the geoid separation added to MSL altitude.

native_goose.desc:
IEC 61850 GOOSE publisher codec (services/energy/goose): the BER IECGoosePdu (gocbRef..allData,
minimal-length INTEGERs with the positive leading-zero rule) + the GOOSE header + Ethernet frame
(ethertype 0x88B8). Pure host tests with structural + spec-derived vectors.

native_gpib.desc:
GPIB-over-LAN (Prologix-style) controller command codec (services/instrumentation/gpib): the ++ command
builders (addr / mode / read / eoi / eos / spoll / clr / trg / ver), the data-line escaping
(leading ESC before CR/LF/ESC/+ in instrument data), the command-vs-data classifier, and the
response parsers (address, serial-poll status byte, version). Pure host tests.

native_gpio_map.desc:
GPIO pin-mapper / browser diag core (server/signaling/gpio_map): direction names, JSON
serializer, control-POST parser, output guard - all pure and host-tested.

native_graphql_exec.desc: GraphQL executor (services/iot/graphql), GraphQL spec October 2021 release: the sec 1 Example No. 3 / No. 4 query and result pair, the sec 2.3 query shorthand, sec 2.4 selection-set order, sec 2.5 nesting, sec 2.6 arguments (in scope down the path, unordered, read by name and scalar kind), the sec 7.1.1 data entry and sec 7.2.1 JSON forms of the sec 3.5 scalars, and the sec 7.1.2 request errors for malformed and out-of-scope grammar (mutations, fragments, variables, directives, aliases, list and input-object values) plus the compile-time bounds. Pure host tests.

native_grpcweb_frame.desc: gRPC-Web framing codec (services/iot/grpcweb), grpc/grpc doc/PROTOCOL-HTTP2.md and doc/PROTOCOL-WEB.md: the Length-Prefixed-Message (Compressed-Flag, 4-byte big-endian Message-Length, Message), the 8th (MSB) trailers bit with the published 10000000b / 10000001b spellings, the trailer-section as RFC 9112 sec 7.1.2 field-lines with lower-case grpc-status / grpc-message names, the 1*DIGIT Status round trip over the gRPC status codes, the Percent-Encoded Status-Message slice, the partial-frame wait and the fail-closed short-buffer refusals. Pure host tests.

native_guardrails.desc:
Heap/stack guardrails (server/core/guardrails): threshold evaluator + JSON,
host-tested. Live sampling is ESP32-only (#ifdef ARDUINO).

native_boot.desc: The reset handler's loops (core_setup/boot): the .data copy, the .bss zero and the stack paint that protocore_platform_stack_free() reads back. Host-run, so the same loops the silicon runs are exercised against caller-supplied regions carrying guard words on both ends.

native_h2conn.desc:
HTTP/2 connection engine (network_drivers/presentation/http/http2/h2_conn, RFC 9113):
initial SETTINGS on init, preface + client SETTINGS -> SETTINGS ACK, decoding a real
HPACK-encoded request into the header callbacks, PING -> PING ACK, split-across-reads frame
reassembly, and h2_conn_respond serializing a HEADERS + DATA response decoded back.

native_h2_frame_rfc.desc: HTTP/2 binary framing (network_drivers/presentation/http/http2/h2_frame, RFC 9113): the 24-octet client connection preface printed in hex by sec 3.4, the sec 4.1 nine-octet frame header field layout and its reserved bit, the 24-bit Length bound, the sec 6.5.2 SETTINGS initial values and the three ranges that section states in words (ENABLE_PUSH, INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE, MAX_FRAME_SIZE), the SETTINGS payload round trip, and the exact octets of the SETTINGS-ACK / WINDOW_UPDATE / RST_STREAM / GOAWAY / PING-ACK / HEADERS / DATA builders against the sec 6 figures, plus the sec 6 type codes and sec 7 error codes.

native_h2server.desc:
HTTP/2 -> request-pipeline bridge (network_drivers/presentation/http/http2/h2_server): the
RFC 9113 sec 8.2 / 8.3 validation a request header block must survive before the route
dispatcher sees it - the mandatory pseudo-header set, duplicates, pseudo-after-regular
ordering, undefined pseudo-headers, field-name and field-value byte rules, and the
connection-specific fields. A rejected block leaves the HttpReq clean and draws an RST_STREAM.
The test owns both ends of the wire through protocore_tls_read / protocore_tls_write.

native_h3_conn.desc:
HTTP/3 application engine (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3/h3_conn, RFC 9114): drives
h3_conn through the quic_conn callback seam - a QPACK-encoded request on a request stream dispatches
the right method/path (+ a POST body), the control stream sends SETTINGS on handshake completion,
and a response (HEADERS + DATA) round-trips through the QUIC stream send buffer.

native_h3_e2e.desc:
End-to-end HTTP/3 capstone (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3): a QUIC client in the
test completes the TLS 1.3 handshake against a quic_conn + h3_conn server, sends a real HTTP/3 GET
(QPACK HEADERS in a STREAM frame), and verifies the app-served response (HEADERS :status 200 + DATA
body) - the whole stack composed: QUIC crypto/framing, TLS 1.3, streams, HTTP/3 framing, QPACK.

native_h3_server.desc:
HTTP/3 dispatch bridge end-to-end through PC (the full Layer-7 app built with
PROTOCORE_ENABLE_HTTP3=1): a QUIC client completes the handshake and sends an HTTP/3 GET, quic_server
routes it to the reserved dispatch slot, match_and_execute runs the registered route, and the
handler's send() is routed back onto the request stream via protocore_quic_server_respond. Verifies the whole
wire: a real route handler answers an HTTP/3 request. Reuses the native_stack_http full-app base.

native_h3_frame_rfc.desc: HTTP/3 framing (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3/h3_frame, RFC 9114 sec 7): the type+length varint header driven through all four sample varint sequences RFC 9000 Appendix A.1 publishes, the long-form spelling that decodes but is never emitted, the sec 11.2.1 frame type registry and its reserved HTTP/2 codes, the sec 7.2.4.1 and RFC 9204 sec 5 settings defaults, the sec 11.2.2 reserved settings identifiers, a SETTINGS round trip with a greased identifier, the DATA / HEADERS / GOAWAY builders, and the truncation and short-destination refusals.

native_haas_mdc.desc:
Haas Machine Data Collection (MDC) Q-command codec (services/machine_tool/haas_mdc): the ?Q query
builders (Q100 serial, Q101 software version, Q102 model, Q104 mode, Q300 power-on time, Q500
program + run status + parts counter, Q600 <var> macro/system-variable read) and the parser for the
>-wrapped comma-delimited responses plus the unprompted DPRNT(...) lines. Pure host tests.

native_happy_eyeballs.desc:
Dual-stack Happy Eyeballs selection (network_drivers/transport/happy_eyeballs): RFC 6724 destination
preference scoring, the candidate-list sort + RFC 8305 address-family interleave, and the Connection
Attempt Delay gate, over the shipped protocore_ip. Pure host tests.

native_hart.desc:
HART / HART-IP codec (services/fieldbus/hart): the HART command frame (longitudinal XOR checksum,
short + long addressing) build/parse and the 8-octet HART-IP message header. Pure host tests with
hand-verified vectors (command-0 checksum 0x82).

native_hex.desc:
Base-16 conversion (shared/hex): the shared digit tables asserted against the ASCII code
points, nibble/character lookup both cases, encode/decode round trip, the odd-length and
overflow refusals, and the RFC 9112 sec 7.1 chunk-size form u32 writes. Pure host tests.

native_hislip.desc:
HiSLIP (High-Speed LAN Instrument Protocol, IVI-6.1) message codec (services/instrumentation/hislip):
the fixed 16-byte header build/parse (HS prologue + type + control + 32-bit param + 64-bit
payload length, big-endian), the Initialize / AsyncInitialize handshake helpers, and the
Data / DataEND SCPI-payload framing with message ids. Pure host tests.

native_hmmd.desc:
Waveshare HMMD 24GHz mmWave micro-motion radar codec (server/peripherals/hmmd): the LD2410-family
little-endian framing, the report parse (detection flag, distance, all 16 gate energies), rejecting
malformed frames, the byte-by-byte stream reassembler (resync past noise, split feeds, absurd-length
drop), the exact bytes of the command encoders (open/close command mode, firmware 0x0000, serial
0x0011, config 0x0008, register 0x0002), and ACK decoding. Pure - the UART pump is ESP32-only.

native_hostlink.desc:
Omron Host Link (C-mode) frame codec (services/fieldbus/hostlink): the FCS (XOR), the ASCII
command builder (@UU + header + text + FCS + *CR), and the FCS-validating parser +
end-code reader. Pure host tests.

native_hotswap.desc:
Removable-storage hot-swap safeties (server/storage/hotswap): the ABSENT/READY/FAULTED state
machine - a run of consecutive I/O errors faults a volume while a single one does not, any success
resets the run, the fail counter saturates instead of wrapping, probe attempts are rate-limited (and
wrap-safe across a millis() rollover), present-but-unmountable stays absent, and a full
removal/reinsertion cycle returns to a clean mount. Pure host tests with a synthetic clock.

native_hpack.desc:
HPACK header compression for HTTP/2 (RFC 7541): prefix-integer coding (App C.1), the
Huffman string code (App B / C.4.1), the first-request decode with dynamic-table insertion
(C.3.1), dynamic-table indexing + FIFO eviction + size updates, and the server encoder
(static indexing + literal round-trip). Pure host codec.

native_codec_hpack_prim.desc: The field-coding primitives HPACK and QPACK share (network_drivers/presentation/codec/hpack_prim) against RFC 7541, which RFC 9204 sec 5 hands QPACK verbatim. The load-bearing case transcribes Appendix B, the code and bit length published for all 256 octets, and drives every symbol through both directions against the RFC's own bits so the encoder and the decoder are each checked against the standard rather than against each other. Around it: Appendix C.1's three worked prefix-integer examples, prefix flags surviving a round trip, every prefix width at and either side of 2^N-1, the sec 5.1 requirement that an integer past the implementation's limit MUST be a decoding error, the Huffman-coded string literals printed in Appendix C.4 and C.6, the sec 5.2 refusals of a decoded EOS symbol and of padding that is too long or not the EOS prefix, both spellings of a string literal read back through the cursor, and the encoder taking whichever of the two forms is shorter.

native_http_client.desc:
Outbound HTTP client: URL parser + request builder + response parser. Pure
string logic (the lwIP/mbedTLS transport is ESP32-only) so it unit-tests host.

native_http_client_session.desc: HTTP client with a net stack: the connection arm and its storage borrow, which the codec env compiles away

native_http_date.desc:
IMF-fixdate formatter (shared/http_date): the RFC 9110 sec 5.6.7 preferred format,
its fixed 29-octet width, the case-sensitive US-ASCII day and month names, and the
empty-rather-than-partial contract for a short buffer. Pure host tests.

native_http_delivery.desc:
HTTP delivery optimizations (services/file_transfer/http_delivery): the RFC 5861 stale-while-revalidate
freshness decision + its Cache-Control builder, and the versioned service-worker precache manifest
(including that a full PROTOCORE_DELIVERY_PRECACHE_MAX manifest fits PROTOCORE_DELIVERY_MANIFEST_BUF and that an
oversized one fails closed rather than truncating). Byte-range serving is network_drivers/application/http_range.h's job,
not this service's. Pure host tests.

native_httpcache.desc:
HTTP Cache-Control helpers (network_drivers/presentation/http/httpcache, RFC 9111 + 8246 + 5861): the
structured directive builder + first-class origin presets (immutable asset / shared / no-store /
revalidatable), the tolerant directive parser (case-insensitive, quoted deltas, unknown ignored),
and the RFC 9111 freshness-lifetime precedence. Pure host tests incl. a build->parse round-trip.

native_hw_health.desc:
Hardware-health diagnostics (server/signaling/hw_health): power-rail voltage-drop logger (worst
droop + sag/brownout counts), SPI-bus CRC audit with hysteretic clock backoff, GPIO short-circuit test
(driven vs readback), and capacitor-leakage diag (measured vs expected RC decay). Pure host tests.

native_iccp.desc:
ICCP / TASE.2 (IEC 60870-6) Data_Value codec (services/energy/iccp): the StateQ (state + quality)
and RealQ (scaled INTEGER + quality) indication-point BER structures with optional timestamp. Pure
host tests with spec-derived vectors.

native_iec60870.desc:
IEC 60870-5-101/-104 codec (services/energy/iec60870): the -104 APCI (I/S/U), the ASDU
header + 3-octet IOA, and the -101 FT1.2 fixed/variable link frames (sum checksum). Pure
host tests.

native_iface_bridge.desc:
Interface bridge pure core (server/net/iface_bridge): the user-defined address:port -> bus
rule table (register / find / dedup / capacity, keyed by port+proto with the full protocore_ip bind address
preserved) and the write-then-read transaction frame codec (big-endian write_len/read_len header,
partial-frame handling, build/parse round-trip). Bus I/O + listener are ESP32-only. Pure host tests.

native_iface_bridge_hw.desc: Interface-bridge glue bind table (server/net/iface_bridge/iface_bridge_hw): publish walking the pure rule table into a listener bind, the null-target and duplicate-port refusals, the table bound, and reset. The suite includes iface_bridge_hw.c so its file-static bind lookup is reachable, which is why the env does not build that .c itself.

native_ikev2.desc:
IKEv2 (RFC 7296) message + payload codec (services/security/ikev2): the 28-octet IKE header, the generic
payload chain walker, the SA -> proposal -> transform tree (incl. the key-length attribute), and the
KE / Nonce / Notify / Delete / IDi-IDr / AUTH / CERT / TSi-TSr / SK-envelope build + parse. Byte-exact
golden vectors generated by scapy's IKEv2 codec (key-length attribute verified against scapy's
decoder). Pure host tests.

native_ikev2_rfc7296.desc:
IKEv2 message and payload codec (services/security/ikev2/ikev2.c). Every expected octet is read
off an RFC 7296 field diagram: sec 3.1 the 28-octet IKE header, sec 3.2 the generic payload header
and the chain walk, sec 3.3-3.3.5 the SA / Proposal / Transform tree with the Key Length attribute
in TV form, sec 3.4 KE, sec 3.5 ID, sec 3.8 AUTH, sec 3.9 Nonce, sec 3.10 Notify, sec 3.11 Delete,
sec 3.13 Traffic Selectors, sec 3.15 Configuration, and sec 3.14 / RFC 5282 sec 3 the Encrypted
envelope. The Curve25519 exchange (Group Num 31, RFC 8031 sec 3) is checked against RFC 7748
sec 6.1's published X25519 vector, and sec 2.13 key lengths, prf+ and the sec 2.6 stateless cookie
round out the suite.

native_ikev2_natt_rfc3948.desc:
IKEv2 NAT traversal (services/security/ikev2/ikev2_natt.c). The NAT_DETECTION_SOURCE_IP and
NAT_DETECTION_DESTINATION_IP payloads are checked octet by octet against RFC 7296 sec 3.10's Notify
layout and sec 3.10.1's Message Types 16388 / 16389, and the port 4500 demux against RFC 3948
sec 2.2's Non-ESP Marker and sec 2.3's 0xFF keepalive. No standard publishes a worked NAT-detection
digest, so the SHA-1 cases are properties: 20 octets, SPIi then SPIr then address then port big
endian, and every one of those inputs changes the value.

native_ina219.desc: INA219 current / power monitor (server/peripherals/ina219): decoding the bus-voltage register (bits 15:3, LSB 4 mV) and the signed shunt register (LSB 10 uV), computing the calibration register from the current LSB and shunt resistance, scaling the raw current / power registers by that LSB, and reading a part end to end - the suite applies a shunt drop and a bus voltage to the SBOS448G device model in core_setup/hal/host/devices/ and the part computes current and power from them by Eq 4 and Eq 5.

native_codec_inflate.desc: The RFC 1951 INFLATE core (network_drivers/presentation/codec/inflate), the WebSocket permessage-deflate receiver. The load-bearing case assembles its streams bit by bit from the RFC itself - sec 3.2.3's block header, sec 3.2.4's stored block with its ones-complement NLEN, sec 3.2.6's fixed code table, sec 3.2.5's length and distance codes and sec 3.1.1's bit order - with the derivation written beside each octet, so nothing there was produced by a compressor and copied back. One dynamic-Huffman block (sec 3.2.7) carries its own code lengths and cannot be hand packed, so its octets come from a reference encoder while the expected value stays the plaintext that went in. The refusals are the RFC's own statements: BTYPE 11 is reserved, NLEN must be the complement of LEN, literal/length 286-287 and distance 30-31 never occur, a distance may not reach before the start of the output, and a stream that ends mid-block is incomplete. Also the permessage-deflate payload with RFC 7692 sec 7.2.2's marker appended, two blocks concatenating, and the output and scratch bounds.

native_interbus.desc:
INTERBUS summation-frame codec (services/fieldbus/interbus): the summation frame (loopback +
per-device 16-bit slices + CRC-16/CCITT FCS) assemble + disassemble. Pure host tests (FCS 0x29B1).

native_iolink.desc:
IO-Link (SDCI) data-link message codec (services/fieldbus/iolink): the MC / CKT / CKS control
octets and the SDCI checksum (seed 0x52 + the 8->6 compression of IO-Link spec A.1.6), with a
hand-computed known-answer vector. Pure host tests.

native_ip.desc:
IP address core (network_drivers/network/protocore_ip): RFC 4291 IPv4/IPv6 text parsing,
RFC 5952 canonical formatting (:: zero-compression, v4-mapped), and scope classification
(loopback / link-local / private-ULA / multicast / global). Pure host tests.

native_system_ipsec_db.desc: IPsec SPD + SAD (services/system/esp/ipsec_db): RFC 4301 sec 4.4.1 ordered first-match policy lookup over overlapping selectors, inclusive address and port ranges compared as whole addresses across IPv4 and IPv6, family mismatch refusal, sec 4.4.4.1 default-deny on no match, bounded policy storage, sec 4.4.1.2 SPD selector built from an IKEv2 TSi/TSr pair, sec 4.4.2 SPI-keyed SAD add/find/remove with duplicate-SPI refusal, per-SA anti-replay windows, and RFC 4303 sec 3.3.3 outbound sequence numbering from 1 with the cycle refused.

native_j1939.desc:
SAE J1939 codec (services/fieldbus/j1939): 29-bit id encode/decode (PDU1 + PDU2), single-frame
messages, Request PGN, Address Claimed + NAME, and the Transport Protocol (BAM + TP.DT)
reassembler, over the shared CAN frame. Pure host tests.

native_j2735_uper.desc: SAE J2735 V2X codec (services/transportation/j2735): the ASN.1 UPER primitive layer against ITU-T X.691 clause 13 (a constrained whole number is the offset from the lower bound in ceil(log2(range)) bits, MSB-first, no inter-field padding) and the BSMcore / SPaT MovementState / MAP intersection encode and decode. The load-bearing case is the 162-bit / 21-octet BSMcore layout asserted against a hand-written bit string. Pure host tests.

native_json_codec.desc: Zero-heap JSON writer and top-level reader (network_drivers/presentation/codec/json, RFC 8259): the sec 13 example object built byte for byte, the sec 7 mandatory escape set, the sec 7 "\uD834\uDD1E" G clef surrogate pair decoded to its RFC 3629 UTF-8 form, the sec 8.2 unpaired surrogate mapped to U+FFFD, the sec 3 literal names, top-level-only member matching, write/read round trip, and the overflow / depth / null-storage refusals.

native_jwt_rfc7515.desc:
HS256 JWT verifier (services/security/jwt). Anchored on RFC 7515 Appendix A.1's complete example:
the token, the symmetric JWK and the MAC all come from the RFC, so the HMAC is judged against a
signature this library did not produce. Also RFC 7515 sec 4.1.1 + RFC 8725 sec 3.1 algorithm
enforcement (alg none / RS256 / HS384 / absent), sec 7.1 serialization shape, RFC 6750 sec 2.1
Bearer credentials with the RFC 7235 sec 2.1 case-insensitive scheme, RFC 7519 sec 4.1.4 / 4.1.5
exp and nbf with skew leeway, sec 4.1.6 iat, and RFC 6749 sec 3.3 whole-token scope matching.

native_keepalive.desc:
HTTP/1.1 keep-alive (persistent connections): full server built with
PROTOCORE_ENABLE_KEEPALIVE=1; a small per-connection request cap makes the
fairness-bound test fast. Drives requests through the real transport ring +
tcp_write capture mock.

native_ld2410.desc:
LD2410 mmWave radar codec (server/peripherals/ld2410): decoding a basic and an engineering-mode
report frame, rejecting malformed frames, the byte-by-byte stream reassembler (resync past
noise, split feeds, absurd-length drop), the presence/distance helpers, and the exact bytes
of the config-command encoders. Pure - the UART pump is ESP32-only.

native_ldc1614.desc:
LDC1614 inductance-to-digital field sensor (server/peripherals/ldc1614): the 28-bit data combine +
error flags, the frequency scale (data/2^28 * fref), and the single-channel config-sequence builder.
Pure codec host tests (the I2C binding is ESP32-only).

native_lfs_mock.desc:
The littlefs-backed protocore_mnt_backend used by the host tests that need a real tree
(core_setup/hal/host/lfs_mock.h): round-trip, seek, directory listing, stat, rename/remove,
append, and a full volume refusing rather than pretending. Real littlefs on a RAM
block device, so the host answers the way the device does.

native_link_manager.desc:
Multi-interface egress selection (server/signaling/link_manager): a table of interfaces (kind +
priority + up/down) with deterministic best-link-up selection, graceful escalation to a higher-priority
interface, failover when it drops, and real-transition change detection. Pure host tests.

native_log_frames.desc: Abstract logging macros (shared/log) whose disabled levels are discarded by the preprocessor: built at PROTOCORE_LOG_LEVEL_INFO so DEBUG is below the floor. Asserts that a discarded call reaches neither the sink nor the ring AND never evaluates its arguments (the whole point of a preprocessor filter over a runtime level check), that INFO/WARN/ERROR emit at their own severity, that the emitted line is the frame the spec builds, that the PROTOCORE_LOG_LEVEL_* and logbuf severity scales agree, and that a mismatched or over-long frame emits an empty line rather than a truncated one. Pure host tests.

native_logbuf.desc: Rotating log ring + severity trap (server/logbuf): pure, fully host-tested.

native_lonworks.desc:
LonWorks / LON-IP network-variable codec (services/fieldbus/lonworks): the LonTalk NV PDU
([msg-code][14-bit selector][value]) build + parse and the SNVT_temp / SNVT_switch scalar encodings.
Pure host tests.

native_lora.desc:
LoRa codec + SX127x driver (services/radio/lora), v5 radio plugin: the RadioHead 4-byte
header parse/build, and the SX127x register protocol (init / send / tx-done / set-rx /
recv) exercised against a mock chip - a register file plus a FIFO with the auto-
incrementing address pointer. Pure host tests; the RF link needs the module.

native_lsv2.desc:
Heidenhain LSV/2 telegram codec (services/machine_tool/lsv2): the framer (4-byte big-endian payload-length
prefix + 4-char mnemonic + payload), the typed request builders (login A_LG / logout A_LO,
null-terminated-filename file commands, R_RI run-info with a 2-byte big-endian selector), and the
response readers (T_OK, the T_ER/T_BD 2-byte error-class + error-code, data replies, stream
re-framing). Byte-exact vectors cross-checked against pyLSV2. Pure host tests.

native_lwm2m_tlv_codec.desc: OMA LwM2M TLV codec (services/iot/lwm2m), OMA-TS-LightweightM2M_Core-V1_2-20201110-A sec 7.4.5: the Table 7.4.5.-1 Type byte (Identifier type in bits 7-6, 8/16-bit Identifier in bit 5, Length-field width in bits 4-3, inline Length in bits 2-0), entries of the sec 7.4.5.1 Read /3/0 Device Object payload reproduced octet for octet, the whole 38-octet sec 7.4.5.2 B) Read /2 Access Control payload parsed three levels deep including its 16-bit Identifier, and the Appendix C Table C.-2 Value forms (shortest signed Integer width, one-octet Boolean, binary64 Float, two's complement sign extension). Pure host tests.

native_mbplus.desc:
Modbus Plus HDLC token-bus codec (services/fieldbus/mbplus): the HDLC frame (7E addr ctrl payload
CRC-16/X-25 7E) build + validate and the token-rotation ring helper. Pure host tests (CRC 0x906E).

native_mbus.desc: Wired M-Bus (EN 13757-2/-3) frame + data-record codec (services/fieldbus/mbus): the single-character / short / long frame builders and the checksum-validating parser, the DIF/VIF record walk with its DIFE+VIFE extension chains, integer / BCD / REAL32 value decoding, the VIF unit + exponent table, and the 12-octet variable-data fixed header. Anchored on the complete RSP_UD telegram worked in M-Bus Usergroup doc rev 4.8 ch. 6.3.3, plus the field, telegram-format and VIF tables of ch. 5.2, 5.3, 6.3 and 8.4. Pure host tests.

native_mdns_adaptive.desc:
Adaptive mDNS beacon scheduling (network_drivers/application/mdns_adaptive): RF-contention backoff/recovery
of the announce interval, the TTL/2 continuous-refresher cadence, the announce-due check, and the
auto-sleep beacon (announce before a sleep that would lapse the record). Wrap-safe. Pure host tests.

native_mdns_service.desc:
The portable mDNS / DNS-SD responder (network_drivers/application/mdns_service, RFC 6762 /
RFC 6763) on the build where PROTOCORE_HAS_VENDOR_MDNS is 0: joining 224.0.0.251:5353 through the UDP
listener, and answering a query for the service-enumeration name, a service type, and an instance's
SRV / TXT - each answer read back off the wire and decoded by the test's own label reader.

native_melsec.desc: Mitsubishi MELSEC MC protocol binary 3E codec (services/fieldbus/melsec): the batch read / batch write request builders (little-endian routing, request data length, command + subcommand, 3-octet head device, device code, point count) and the response parser (subheader, length field, end code, read data). Anchored on the worked binary 3E request and response of the MELSEC Communication Protocol Reference Manual SH(NA)-080008 appendix 7, its ch. 8.1 device code list and its ch. 5.3 field definitions. Pure host tests.

native_membuild.desc:
The bounded no-heap builder (mmgr/membuild.h): bump-append into a caller-owned
region with ok latching false the first time something would not fit, so the caller tests one flag
at the end instead of a return per call. Covers that the capacity reserves a byte for the
terminator, that a refused append writes nothing and every later append is a no-op, that a
zero-capacity builder does not even write the terminator, and the two clipping appenders that
deliberately do NOT latch - byte-wise for display text, all-or-nothing for a number, since half a
number reads as a different number. The renderings are diffed against libc printf, which is what
they replace: %llu, %llx and %0Nu across the 32-bit fast path and the value just past it, %lld
including the minimum where negating the value would overflow, %.<sig>g at every precision from 1
to 10 over both signs of a value set that includes the rounding ties, the decade carries, the
subnormals and the exponent extremes, and %.<n>f over the range that form occupies. Plus the sign
bit read for negative zero, the infinity and NaN words, and the XML and JSON escapes.

native_mmgr_membuild.desc: Bounded builder (mmgr/membuild.h): the zero-padded integer conversions of ISO C11 sec 7.21.6.1 at bases 8, 10 and 16, the XML 1.0 sec 4.6 predefined entities, the RFC 8259 sec 7 JSON string escapes, and the IEEE 754 sec 3.4 sign/inf/NaN predicates. The load-bearing case is the latch: one append that would not fit makes every later append a no-op and makes finish report zero, which is what lets a caller test one flag at the end instead of a return value per call.

native_mms.desc:
IEC 61850 MMS PDU codec (services/energy/mms): the BER confirmed-request/response Read PDUs
(invokeID + read service + named ObjectName), build + parse. Pure host tests with structural vectors.

native_mnt.desc:
Mounted storage (server/storage/mnt) - the backend vtable and its built-in RAM backend,
host-tested through that backend (the Arduino FS backend is board-layer and HW-verified).
Files, directories, stat, and the readdir cursor. Pure, no heap.

native_modbus.desc: Modbus TCP slave core + RTU framing (services/fieldbus/modbus): the four-table data model, the MBAP header validation and echo, and the PDU dispatch for function codes 01 02 03 04 05 06 0F 10 16 17 with their exception responses. Every request/response pair is the worked example printed in Modbus Application Protocol V1.1b3 sec. 6.1-6.12, 6.16, 6.17 and sec. 7; the MBAP rules are Modbus Messaging on TCP/IP V1.0b sec. 3.1.3. The RTU arm covers CRC-16 validation, unit addressing and the silent broadcast. Data model widened to 256 entries so the spec's own addresses are in range. Pure host tests.

native_modbus_master.desc:
Modbus master codec + scanner (services/fieldbus/modbus/modbus_master): build read
requests, parse responses; host-tested as a round-trip against the slave codec.

native_mpr121.desc: MPR121 12-channel capacitive touch (server/peripherals/mpr121): decoding the two touch-status registers (ELEPROX at D4 and OVCF at D7 sit above the twelve electrodes), the 10-bit filtered-data pair, the AN3944 bring-up sequence builder, and programming a part end to end - the suite reads the registers back off the device model in core_setup/hal/host/devices/, where section 5.1 discards any configuration write made outside Stop Mode.

native_mqtt_codec.desc: MQTT Control Packet codec (services/iot/mqtt), OASIS MQTT 3.1.1: the sec 2.2.3 Table 2.4 Remaining Length boundaries with the octets the table prints, the sec 3.1.2 Figure 3.2 / 3.3 / 3.6 CONNECT Protocol Name, Level, Connect Flags and Keep Alive with the MQTT-3.1.3-1 payload order, the sec 3.3.2.3 Figure 3.11 PUBLISH variable header, the sec 3.8.3.1 Figure 3.23 SUBSCRIBE payload, the Table 2.1 type values and Table 2.2 reserved flag bits, the Table 3.1 Connect Return codes and sec 3.9.3 SUBACK codes, and the MQTT-3.3.2-2 wildcard / MQTT-3.3.1-4 QoS / MQTT-1.5.3 UTF-8 refusals. Pure host tests.

native_mqtt_session.desc: MQTT with a net stack: the session arm, its storage borrow and the transport half the codec env compiles away

native_mqtt_sn_codec.desc: MQTT-SN v1.2 wire codec (services/iot/mqtt/mqtt_sn.c), MQTT-SN Protocol Specification Version 1.2 (Stanford-Clark and Truong, IBM, 2013): the sec 5.2.1 Length field and its 1-octet / 3-octet boundary at 255, the sec 5.2.2 Table 3 MsgType octets, the sec 5.3.4 Table 4 Flags bit positions and TopicIdType, the sec 5.3.10 Table 5 ReturnCodes, and the sec 5.4 Message Variable Parts of CONNECT / CONNACK / REGISTER / REGACK / PUBLISH / PUBACK / SUBSCRIBE / SUBACK / PINGREQ / DISCONNECT / SEARCHGW with their optional fields and their fail-closed refusals. Pure host tests.

native_msgpack_wire.desc: MessagePack codec (network_drivers/presentation/codec/msgpack): every family's first byte taken from the specification's own format overview table (positive/negative fixint, uint/int 8-64, fixstr and str 8/16/32, bin 8/16, fixarray/array 16, fixmap/map 16, nil, false, true, float 32) at each range boundary the table states, the IEEE 754 single and double bit patterns behind 0xca / 0xcb, peek's first-byte-to-type mapping including the never-used 0xc1 and the ext family, decode of every integer width, str/bin views that alias the input, map and array round trips, truncation and sticky-error refusals, and the overflow counter that reports the capacity a buffer should have had.

native_mtconnect.desc:
MTConnect agent response codec (services/machine_tool/mtconnect, ANSI/MTC1.4): the incremental
MTConnectStreams builder (header + Samples/Events/Condition), the MTConnectDevices probe (device
model), the MTConnectAssets response (CuttingTool life cycle), the sample sequence cursor (a rolling
observation ring replayed as a from/count long-poll window), and the MTConnectError document,
XML-escaped. Pure host tests with structural assertions.

native_net_addr.desc: net_addr: the stack address <-> protocore_ip mapping. Both directions for both families, the refusals (null source, null destination, untagged family, empty address), the byte order each direction lands in, and the NetAddr entries, which no call site in src/ reaches.

native_nats_proto.desc: NATS client protocol codec (services/iot/nats), NATS Protocol client reference (docs.nats.io): the published PUB / HPUB / SUB / UNSUB / PING / PONG / CONNECT builder examples reproduced character for character with their #bytes and #header bytes / #total bytes counts, the MSG / HMSG / INFO / -ERR / +OK parser over the same published examples, the Protocol conventions field delimiter (space or tab, repeated whitespace as one), the wait-for-the-whole-operation framing and the fail-closed builder refusals. Pure host tests.

native_nema_ts2_sdlc.desc: NEMA TS 2 traffic-cabinet SDLC frame codec (services/transportation/nema_ts2): the [address][control][frame-type][data][FCS-16] build and validate.
