The FCS is CRC-16/X-25, so a frame spelling the catalogue check input '123456789' must carry 6E 90 (check value 0x906E, low octet first), and RFC 1662 sec C.2's good-FCS residue over the frame including its own FCS pins both the parameters and the transmission order. Plus single-bit error detection over every bit. Pure host tests.

native_net_egress.desc:
Egress-interface reporting (network_drivers/physical). The esp_netif default-
route lookups are ESP32-only; the pure interface-key classifier host-tests here.

native_l1_egress.desc: Egress-interface reporting with no L1 backend (network_drivers/physical). RFC 1122 sec 3.3.1.2 makes the default route the interface outbound traffic leaves by, so the classifier that maps a live default-route IPv4 against the station and softAP addresses is the one call whose answer varies with its input: each arm returns a different protocore_if_kind, an interface that is down carries address 0 and never claims the route, and the station is compared before the softAP. The addresses are RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1 in the network byte order of RFC 791 appendix B. The rest pins the PROTOCORE_PHYSICAL_HAS_BACKEND == 0 build: bring-up with nothing to do reports success while the link never comes ready, every readout answers its not-available value, and the two RFC 826 six-octet hardware address readouts refuse without writing into the caller's buffer.

native_netadapt.desc:
Network adaptation decisions (server/net/netadapt): TCP receive-window sizing from the free
heap (reserve + quarter-of-spare, clamped) and the DHCP->static-IP fallback trigger. Pure host tests.

native_gnss_nmea0183.desc: NMEA 0183 sentence codec (services/timing_position/nmea0183): the eight complete worked sentences the gpsd NMEA reference publishes, each accepted and each rejected under every single-character edit, the XOR checksum folded by hand for two of them, sentence framing and the AIS delimiter, field splitting with empty fields counted, and the typed decoders for GGA/RMC/GSV/ZDA/VTG/GSA/GLL/DPT plus MWV/HDG/VHW/VLW round trips, including ddmm.mmmm to signed decimal degrees and the E/W sign folding.

native_marine_nmea2000.desc: NMEA 2000 codec (services/timing_position/nmea2000): the Fast Packet transport (frame count from the 6 + 7n split, the sequence and frame counters packed in the control octet, split and byte-for-byte reassembly up to 223 octets, out-of-order and foreign-sequence rejection, bounds), single-frame build over the J1939 29-bit identifier, and the typed PGN decoders with their documented scalings and not-available sentinels (position, COG/SOG, engine rapid and dynamic, wind, depth, heading, attitude, temperature Kelvin-to-Celsius, battery). NMEA 2000 is not a public document, so expectations are properties plus the scalings the header states.

native_nrf24.desc:
nRF24L01+ driver (services/radio/nrf24), v5 radio plugin: the Nordic SPI command protocol
(STATUS shifted out first, W/R_REGISTER, W_TX/R_RX_PAYLOAD, write-1-to-clear) exercised
against a mock chip - init / send (padded to the static width) / tx-done / set-rx / recv
(pipe-addressed). Pure host tests; the RF link needs the module.

native_ntcip_oid.desc: NTCIP transportation-device object OIDs (services/transportation/ntcip): every object root is asserted to sit under 1.3.6.1.4.1.1206.4.2, which is RFC 2578 sec 4's enterprises arc plus the IANA Private Enterprise Number 1206 (NEMA), and the 1202 signal-controller and 1203 DMS subtrees are asserted distinct. Plus the OID builder (root + instance index), its buffer guard and its null guards. Pure host tests.

native_ntp_server.desc:
NTP/SNTP server (RFC 5905 server mode): the response codec (ntp_server_build_response) -
version echo, mode/LI/stratum, origin-timestamp copy, reference/receive/transmit stamps,
big-endian encoding, and the length guards - plus the UDP/123 bind and its handler, driven
through the host stack's pcb so the reply that reaches the wire is the one a client would get.

native_ntp_service.desc:
The SNTP client (network_drivers/application/ntp_service, RFC 4330), which is the client on
every target: the mode-3 request it puts on the wire, the mode-4 reply it accepts, and the ones it
refuses - a wrong mode, a kiss-o'-death stratum, an origin that does not echo the request's transmit
stamp, and a pre-2021 clock. Plus the epoch advancing off the monotonic tick between syncs.

native_gnss_ntrip_caster.desc: NTRIP caster protocol codec (services/timing_position/gnss/ntrip_caster): the RFC 9112 sec 2.1 request line and empty-line-terminated header block with every prefix reported incomplete, RFC 9110 sec 5.1 case-insensitive field names, the RFC 7617 sec 2 Basic credential reproduced from its published Aladdin example, NTRIP 1.0 versus 2.0 response forms, the 404 and 401 refusals with a WWW-Authenticate challenge, and the source table's STR record field positions plus a Content-Length that matches the body it declares.

native_nts_ke.desc: Network Time Security wire codec (network_drivers/application/nts, RFC 8915). Covers the NTS-KE record format of sec 4 Figure 2 (the 15-bit Record Type under the Critical Bit, and a Body Length that counts the body alone), the standard client request of secs 4.1.1 / 4.1.2 / 4.1.5 (Next Protocol 0 = NTPv4, AEAD 15 = AES-SIV-CMAC-256, End of Message), the End-of-Message rule that makes a message self-delimiting, and the RFC 7822 sec 3 NTP extension-field framing whose Length counts the entire field including padding to a four-octet word. Record type numbers and the TLS exporter label are checked against RFC 8915 sec 7.

native_oauth2_rfc6749.desc:
OAuth 2.0 token-endpoint client (services/security/oauth2). Anchored on RFC 6749: sec 4.1.3's
Access Token Request body and sec 6's refresh body reproduced with the running example's code,
client id and secret, sec 5.1's token response and sec 5.2's error object parsed, and the RFC 3986
sec 2.1 / 2.3 percent-encoding checked over the unreserved set and the octets outside it. Also the
RFC 7636 sec 4.5 PKCE code_verifier parameter and the all-or-nothing short-buffer refusal.

native_oauth2_exchange.desc: The oauth2 transport calls: the borrow they carve their request body and reply into, and what they report when the exchange never reached an endpoint. PROTOCORE_ENABLE_HTTP_CLIENT is what compiles them at all, and without a net stack HttpClient.post reports HTTP_CLIENT_ERR_CONNECT.

native_oauth2_transport.desc: The oauth2 token exchange over a real transport: the RFC 6749 sec 4.1.3 body goes out through http_client, the host peer answers it, and the sec 5.1 parameters come back out of the module's own reply buffer. The exchange env compiles the same two calls with no net stack, where nothing can answer.

native_observability.desc:
Transport observability (PROTOCORE_ENABLE_OBSERVABILITY): the protocore_conn_on_event
hook, by-reason counters, the live CONN_CLOSING gauge, and that the real lwIP
callbacks (recv FIN / error / timeout / local close / backpressure) drive the
right counter. Pure L4 core - host-tested.

native_ocit_msg.desc: OCIT-Outstations message codec (services/transportation/ocit): the object message [message-type][object-type:2][instance:2][data-type][value] build and parse, with the two 16-bit address fields asserted big-endian on values a swapped pair would read as a different valid object, the typed uint16 accessor and its type/length gate, the octet-string remainder, and the buffer guards. The OCIT-O specification is not obtainable, so these are properties of the documented layout. Pure host tests.

native_oidc_rfc7515.desc:
OpenID Connect RS256 ID Token verifier (services/security/oidc). Anchored on RFC 7515 Appendix
A.2: the RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 SHA-256 token and the 2048-bit RSA JWK that signed it both come from the
RFC, so a real modexp verification runs against a signature this library did not produce. Also
RFC 7517 sec 5.1 JWK Set selection by kid, RFC 7515 sec 4.1.4 kid extraction, and OpenID Connect
Core 1.0 sec 3.1.3.7 steps 2, 3, 7 and 9 (iss, aud, alg RS256, exp).

native_opcua.desc: OPC UA Binary server core (services/fieldbus/opcua): the little-endian built-in type codec, NodeId encoding forms, the UACP header + Hello/Acknowledge/Error handshake, the OpenSecureChannel exchange, the MSG envelope and the CreateSession / ActivateSession / GetEndpoints / Read / Write / Browse / CloseSession / ServiceFault responses, plus Variant and DataValue. Anchored on OPC UA Part 6 sec. 5.2.2 (published byte encodings, the NodeId table) and sec. 7.1.2 (UACP), Part 4 sec. 5.5 / 5.6 / 5.8 / 5.10, and the OPC Foundation NodeIds.csv + StatusCode.csv registry values. Pure host tests.

native_openadr.desc:
OpenADR 3.0 JSON codec (services/energy/openadr): the event (programID + eventName + interval
payloads) and report (VEN reading) JSON documents build, with escaping + a no-stdlib 3-decimal
formatter. Pure host tests.

native_ota.desc:
Parser streaming-body hook (OTA) - exercises http_parser with PROTOCORE_ENABLE_OTA=1
using a mock sink (no ESP32 Update dependency).

native_ota_rollback.desc:
OTA rollback decision (server/update/ota_rollback): pure decision matrix host-tested;
the esp_ota commit/rollback are ESP32-only.

native_packml.desc:
PackML / OMAC packaging-machine state model (services/machine_tool/packml), ISA-TR88.00.02: the pure
17-state transition engine (command / state-complete / execute-complete + command validity) and the
owned PackTags service (state advance, production counters, unit-mode rules, machine speed, and the
state/reset timers). Pure host tests.

native_partition.desc:
Flash partition-map monitor (server/storage/partition_monitor core): the kind
classifier + JSON serializer host-test here; the esp_partition walk is ESP32-only.

native_partition_ota.desc: The partition monitor's capability arm: the same suite as native_partition, built with PROTOCORE_HAS_VENDOR_OTA=1 so collect compiles the arm that walks the table through protocore_platform_partition_walk. native_partition drives the other arm, which reports no partitions. Both arms ship, so both are run.

native_pca9685.desc: PCA9685 16-channel 12-bit PWM / servo driver (server/peripherals/pca9685): the PRE_SCALE value for a PWM frequency (Eq 1, hardware minimum 3), the per-channel register base, a servo pulse width as a 12-bit count, the five-byte channel write, and programming a part end to end - the suite reads the registers back off the Rev. 4 device model in core_setup/hal/host/devices/, where a PRE_SCALE write is blocked unless begin() slept the oscillator first.

native_pcap.desc:
libpcap savefile headers (shared/pcap): the 24-octet global header - magic 0xa1b2c3d4 in
file order, version 2.4, snaplen, DLT - and the 16-octet per-record header, each field
read back at its own little-endian offset. Pure host tests.

native_pentest.desc:
Adversarial / pentest harness - run SEPARATELY (`python test/harness.py run native_pentest`), NOT part of the default run. Fuzzes the untrusted-input parsers (HTTP, multipart,
CoAP, SNMP+BER, Modbus, CBOR, MessagePack, JSON, base64/base32, the SQLite
on-disk file-format reader, the Redis RESP reply decoder, the OPC UA Binary
message parsers, the SMB2 client response parsers + the SPNEGO DER walker +
NTLMSSP CHALLENGE, the DNC block decoder, the FTP client reply parsers, and the
industrial client response parsers FINS / MELSEC / CIP / EtherNet-IP / DF1, the
BACnet/IP + ISO-transport TPKT/COTP frame parsers, the IEEE C37.118
synchrophasor + FINS command parsers, the JWT HS256 token verifier, the
DirectNET / CC-Link / AMQP / MMS frame parsers, the DDS/RTPS UDP submessage
walker, the WebDAV (RFC 4918) PROPPATCH body walker + Destination-header
percent-decoder, and the HPACK HTTP/2 + QPACK HTTP/3 header-block decoders) with malformed/oversized/partial/random/mutated input and asserts bounded
buffers + fail-closed + termination (no crash, no over-read, no hang). Pairs with
the live driver penetration_testing/pc_pentest.py. See docs/PENTEST.md.

native_phy.desc:
Layer 1 driven through a REAL backend: the env declares PROTOCORE_PHYSICAL_HAS_BACKEND=1,
so and core_setup/hal/host/physical stands in for silicon instead of the
no-op stubs in physical.c. Nothing else in the tree builds that backend, and without it every L1
readout answers empty - which means a caller that mishandles a live link reads exactly like one
that works, and no assertion can tell them apart. Here the link actually comes up: the station
associates and reports its SSID, channel and a negative dBm RSSI; the softAP takes its own address
without stealing the route; Ethernet then takes the default route from the station, the way a
stack picks one when both are up. That is also the only way to separate the same-signature members
a stub build cannot - eth->init from eth->ready, ip6->init from ip6->ready, and link->mac from
link->egress_mac, which return DIFFERENT addresses once a wired link carries traffic. Addresses
are RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1 and RFC 3849 2001:db8::/32, the MACs are checked for the IEEE 802 U/L and
I/G bits, the SSID cap is IEEE 802.11-2020 9.4.2.2's 32 octets, and a global IPv6 address is
checked not to be an RFC 4291 sec 2.5.6 link-local. PROTOCORE_RADIO_WIFI_PS is set to max modem so the
keep-awake refcount is provable: the first busy_hold forces sleep off and the balancing release
restores the configured mode, which is indistinguishable from the held state at the default of 0.
This is the only env that compiles radio_power.c's backend arm at all.

native_l1_link.desc: Layer 1 driven through a real backend: the env declares PROTOCORE_PHYSICAL_HAS_BACKEND=1, so core_setup/hal/host/physical stands in for silicon instead of the no-op stubs in physical.c, and the link can actually come up. That is what makes the readouts checkable at all, since a stub answers every one of them with an empty value and a caller that mishandles a live link then reads exactly like one that works. The station associates and reports its SSID, its channel and a negative dBm RSSI; the softAP takes its own address without stealing the route; Ethernet then takes the default route from the station the way a stack picks one when both are up. It is also the only way to separate the same-signature calls a stub build cannot: eth_init from eth_ready, ip6_init from ip6_ready, and wifi_mac from egress_mac, which answer with DIFFERENT addresses once a wired link carries traffic. Addresses are RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1 and RFC 3849 2001:db8::/32, the hardware addresses are checked for the RFC 7042 sec 2.1 U/L and I/G bits, the SSID cap is IEEE 802.11-2020 9.4.2.2's 32 octets, and a global unicast IPv6 address (RFC 4291 sec 2.5.4) is checked not to be an RFC 4291 sec 2.5.6 link-local. PROTOCORE_RADIO_WIFI_PS is set to max modem so the keep-awake refcount is provable: the first hold forces doze off and the balancing release restores the configured mode, which at the default of 0 would be indistinguishable from the held state. This is the only env that compiles radio_power.c's backend arm at all.

native_phy_iface.desc:
The layer 1 interface registry (network_drivers/physical, Physical.iface): an interface is
an id, a kind and the callback that puts bytes on the wire, and a device carries several of mixed
kind. Registration and its refusals (duplicate id, null send, table full), the readbacks, reset,
row walking, and that send hands the callback the id and ctx it was registered with. Every
forwarded byte leaves through this send, so it is covered here and not only through forward.

native_plaintext.desc:
The plaintext pool accessor (mmgr/plaintext): bump-allocate + reset semantics,
alignment, and fail-closed exhaustion. Pure host tests - no lwIP/sockets - so it builds from
the accessor and the pool mechanism alone.

native_mmgr_plaintext.desc: Plaintext pool accessor (mmgr/plaintext.h): bump borrow, alignment, the O(1) reset that reuses the base, fail-closed exhaustion, LIFO mark/release, the span form binding the length to the borrow, and the persistent end the per-dispatch reset does not reach. No standard governs a scratch pool, so every expectation is a property. The load-bearing one is a security property: the plaintext and secret pools are disjoint address ranges, so a borrow from one is never claimed by the other.

native_pmbus.desc:
PMBus 1.3 numeric encodings (server/peripherals/pmbus): the VOUT_MODE format selector and its
5-bit signed exponent, the LINEAR11 11-bit signed mantissa and 5-bit signed exponent with decode
and round trip, LINEAR16 against an exponent the part reports separately, the DIRECT coefficient
form, and that a value the exponent pushes out of an int32 of micro-units is refused rather than
wrapped.

native_pn532.desc:
PN532 NFC frame codec (server/peripherals/pn532), v5 radio plugin: the normal-information-frame
build/parse against the documented GetFirmwareVersion command + response frames (LEN/LCS +
DCS checksums), a round trip, malformed framing (bad preamble / start / LCS / DCS), the ACK
frame, and over-length rejection. Pure host tests.

native_pool_workers.desc:
Both pool accessors at PROTOCORE_WORKER_COUNT=2. Slot resolution is unobservable in a single-worker
build - protocore_worker_self() is an inline compile-time 0 there, so a test cannot present any other
identity and every borrow lands on slot 0 whatever the accessor does. Only here does the id
become a real per-task read, so this is the only env in which a worker borrowing from its OWN
slot, and a caller that is not a server worker landing on the ghost instead of colliding with
worker 0, are distinguishable from each other.

native_power_mgmt.desc:
SoC power governor (server/power_mgmt): the pure clock decision from load, die
temperature and reset reason - load-based scaling, the thermal hysteresis that stops a part parked at
the limit from oscillating (asserted by feeding the plan's own output back for 20 ticks and counting
one transition), post-brownout recovery holding the floor even when busy and cool, the precedence
between the three, and INT16_MIN meaning no sensor rather than ice-cold.

native_powerlink.desc: Ethernet POWERLINK basic frame codec (services/fieldbus/powerlink): the SoC / PReq / PRes / SoA / ASnd builders over the [messageType][dest][source][payload] frame, the parser, and the node addressing. Anchored on EPSG DS 301 V1.5.1 App. 3.1 (normative message type ids), sec. 4.5 (node id assignment) and sec. 4.6.1.1 (basic frame structure). Pure host tests.

native_pqc.desc:
Post-quantum hybrid KEX primitives (network_drivers/presentation/pqc): the
Keccak/SHA-3/SHAKE sponge (FIPS 202) and ML-KEM-768 Encaps (FIPS 203) - the responder half of the
mlkem768x25519-sha256 (SSH) and X25519MLKEM768 (TLS 1.3) hybrid key exchanges - plus the full
Streamlined NTRU Prime sntrup761 KEM (keypair/enc/dec) for sntrup761x25519-sha512@openssh.com.
SHA-3/SHAKE digests pinned from NIST FIPS 202 vectors; ML-KEM Encaps byte-checked against a kyber-py
vector; sntrup761 decapsulation checked against an OpenSSH-reference KAT plus a keypair/enc/dec
round-trip. Pure host tests.

native_sha3_kat.desc: Keccak-f[1600] (crypto/hash/sha3.h) against the NIST CAVP FIPS 202 byte-oriented known-answer vectors: SHA3-256, SHA3-512, SHAKE128 and SHAKE256 each at the empty message, a short message, rate-1 octets (where the domain byte and the 0x80 pad merge on one state octet) and exactly one rate, plus a three-block SHA3-256 LongMsg row. Adds the published FIPS 202 rates, SHA-3 / SHAKE domain separation, incremental-squeeze continuity across the rate boundary, and the prefix-stream property.

native_mlkem_kat.desc: ML-KEM-768 (crypto/pqc/mlkem.h) against the NIST ACVP FIPS 203 known-answer vectors for KeyGen, Encaps and Decaps, transcribed into mlkem_acvp_kat.h from NIST's published gen-val JSON. Adds the FIPS 203 Table 2 encoding sizes, the ek and z embedded in dk, KEM correctness across several messages, the sec 6.3 implicit-reject behaviour on a tampered ciphertext, and the sec 7.2 modulus check on a malformed encapsulation key.

native_sntrup761_kat.desc: Streamlined NTRU Prime sntrup761 (crypto/pqc/sntrup761.h). sntrup761 is not standardized, so the one conformance value is an interop vector captured from OpenSSH's embedded reference and it pins Decaps; the rest are properties: KEM round trip over many keypairs, randomized Encaps, the public key embedded in sk at the header's offset, implicit rejection on a tampered rounded polynomial and on a tampered Confirm hash, and the KeyGen retry when g is not invertible mod 3.

native_preempt_queue.desc:
Preempting work queue (server/core/preempt_queue), v5 real-time ingest: FIFO order,
urgent-to-front, fail-closed when full, high-water, and the hand-off from a post to the lane
task's handler. The DMA lane is driven end to end by the host DMA driver (mmgr/dma): a fed
transfer completes where the ISR would fire, its callback posts the bytes onto the lane, and the
lane's task does the work. The post and the task run on the host through the keyed queue mock;
only the interrupt itself and the preempt latency need hardware.

native_primitives.desc:
Shared no-stdlib primitives (shared): the base-10 protocore_strtol/strtoul/strtof
number parsers (numparse.h), the strict RFC 3629 UTF-8 validator (utf8.h), and the parameterized
Rocksoft/Williams CRC engine (crc.h). Every preset is asserted against its published cataloge check
value (the CRC of "123456789"), and the engine is then diffed against the hand-rolled CRC loops the
in-tree services used to carry - X-25, CCITT-FALSE, ARC, MODBUS, DNP, CRC-32, ESP3 CRC-8 and the
Sensirion CRC-8 - across every length 0..64. Those loops are interop-proven against real peers, so
the 13 services now calling the engine are proven byte-identical to the code they retired rather
than merely plausible; the transcriptions here are what still pins that behaviour. Plus the streaming
split, the reflect flags, width masking, and single-bit-flip detection. Header-only; pure host tests.

native_crc.desc: The parameterized Rocksoft/Williams CRC engine (shared/crc). Every one of the thirteen presets is asserted against its published catalogue check value (the CRC of "123456789"), so a wrong polynomial, a swapped init or a flipped reflect flag fails here rather than corrupting a codec. The engine is then diffed against the hand-rolled CRC loops the in-tree services used to carry - X-25, CCITT-FALSE, ARC, MODBUS, DNP, CRC-32, ESP3 CRC-8 and the Sensirion CRC-8 - across every length 0..64, plus the begin/update/final split against the one-shot, width masking, the 8..32 width clamp, and single-bit-flip detection. Pure host tests.

native_mmgr_primitives.desc: No-stdlib floating-point renderers (mmgr/membuild.h Sb.g and Sb.fixed) against ISO C11 sec 7.21.6.1. Every expected string is derived from that clause in the comment beside it rather than captured from a libc run: the g style rule (style f while P greater than X and X at least -4, style e otherwise, then trailing zeros stripped), the two-digit exponent, and the f rounding of the STORED binary value, which is why 2.675 renders 2.67 and 0.05 renders 0.1. Also the documented fallback to the significant-digit form at or above 2^64.

native_profibus.desc: PROFIBUS-DP FDL telegram codec (services/fieldbus/profibus): the FT 1.2 SD1 / SD2 / SD3 builders and the validating parser, the FCS (the arithmetic sum of DA + SA + FC + data unit, carries discarded), the doubled LE length field, and the start / end delimiters. Anchored on the EN 50170 FT 1.2 telegram format tables as reproduced in the PROFIBUS Manual; the FC function-code table could not be obtained, so only the published FC bits (b7 reserved, b6 = request) are asserted. Pure host tests.

native_profinet.desc: PROFINET DCP frame codec (services/fieldbus/profinet): the 12-octet FrameID + DCP header build/parse (ServiceID, ServiceType, Xid, ResponseDelayFactor, DCPDataLength - all big-endian), the option/suboption blocks with their even-length padding, and the block walk. Anchored on the Wireshark PROFINET dissector (plugins/profinet/packet-pn-dcp.c) and the rt-labs p-net pf_dcp_header_t layout, both implementations of IEC 61158-6-10. Pure host tests.

native_promisc_dot11.desc: Wi-Fi promiscuous capture helpers (services/radio/promisc/promisc.c): the IEEE 802.11 MAC header parser against clause 9.2.4.1 Frame Control, the clause 9.3.2 address-field table for all four To DS / From DS combinations, clause 9.2.4.4 sequence control, and the QoS Control and HT Control header extensions; plus the libpcap savefile global and record headers with LINKTYPE_IEEE802_11 105. Pure host tests.

native_protobuf_wire.desc: Protocol Buffers wire codec (services/iot/protobuf), Google's Encoding document: the published Test1 (08 96 01), Test2 (12 07 testing) and Test3 (1a 03 08 96 01) worked examples, the Base 128 varint over its width boundaries, the (field_number << 3) | wire_type tag formula with the wire type ID table, the published ZigZag table for sint32 and sint64 against two's complement int64, the little-endian I32 / I64 payloads and IEEE 754 float / double bit patterns, packed repeated fields, and the refusal of deprecated group and unassigned wire types plus every truncated record. Pure host tests.

native_protomem.desc:
The byte-span walks (mmgr/protomem): copy, move, compare, find, fill, zero, one
register-width load or store per step. cpy and set store a WHOLE word and mask the tail, so the
lanes between n and the end of the word n stops in go to zero - those lanes are the padding of the
borrow, which is what lets the store stay a dumb word instead of a byte walk. Every assertion here
is written against that lane boundary rather than against n, and the destinations are aligned
because a borrow is. Covers every length through two full words, a source at every offset within a
word (the funnel that assembles the wanted word from the two aligned words holding it), both
overlap directions of move, cmp's sign taken from the first differing byte at every position and
ordered as UNSIGNED, cmp and chr not stopping at a NUL because a span has no terminator, chr's
bound and its first-match rule, and the fill splatting a high-bit value into every lane. Plus one
test that each table member is the walk its name says: the table is initialized positionally.

native_mmgr_protomem.desc: Byte-span operations (mmgr/protomem.h) against ISO C11 sec 7.24: memcmp's unsigned-char ordering (sec 7.24.1 p1, so 0x80 orders above 0x7F), memcpy moving exactly n bytes at every source/destination offset pair through the funnel, memmove correct under overlap in both directions, memchr spanning the whole bound rather than stopping at a NUL, and memset/zero touching only their span. Guard bytes either side of every write.

native_protostr.desc:
The bounded-run walks (mmgr/protostr): len, diff, eq, starts, find, has, copy, the
step rungs and the classifiers. The number parsers this module also carries are exercised by
native_primitives against the numparse contract and are only checked for binding here. Covers the
two opposite cap contracts the header draws - len's nul_cap is a WILLINGNESS to keep looking while
every compare's read_cap is a PROMISE that the bytes exist - the first-difference index at every
position and every alignment, equality refusing a prefix where starts accepts it (the same walk
reading the tie the other way), find's first-occurrence rule at every position, its empty needle
matching at the start, and a haystack NUL ending the search since a needle byte is never NUL.
Case folding is checked to touch the letters and NOT '_' vs '?' or '[' vs '{', which differ in the
same bit. copy's bound belongs to the destination and always terminates. find is then diffed
against a naive search written in the test over the inputs that break a search: periodic and
self-overlapping haystacks where a failed match cannot skip the needle's length, needles that are
their own prefix, every substring of the subject taken from every position, a single flipped byte
at every position of a near-miss, and high-bit bytes that a byte compared as signed would order
backwards - each at every offset within a word and under both case rules. Every subject is an
aligned padded region, because that is the only kind of memory the library is ever handed. Plus
one test that each table member is the walk its name says: the table is initialized positionally.

native_mmgr_protostr.desc: Bounded-run operations (mmgr/protostr.h): POSIX.1-2008 strnlen for the bounded length, ISO C11 sec 7.24.4/7.24.5 for the comparison and search semantics, sec 7.4.1.5/7.4.1.10 for the digit and white-space sets, and sec 7.22.1.3/7.22.1.4 for the strtod/strtol endptr contract. The load-bearing case is that the case-insensitive fold applies to ASCII letters alone: bit 5 also separates the underscore from the question mark and the open bracket from the open brace, and folding it everywhere would match a header name or a token against something it is not.

native_prov.desc: First-boot WiFi provisioning / captive portal (server/core/provisioning_service): the x-www-form-urlencoded field parser (whole-name matching, + and %XX decoding, bounded output), and the portal itself - the catch-all DNS answer, the credential load / save / clear through hal/nvs.h, and the softAP address begin() stamps. Extends native_stack_http because the portal registers HTTP routes and binds a UDP port.

native_proxy_protocol.desc:
HAProxy PROXY protocol codec (network_drivers/transport/proxy_protocol): the v1 (text) + v2 (binary)
TCP/IPv4 header builders and the unified parser (recover the real client IP behind a load
balancer). Pure host tests.

native_psram_pool.desc:
Buffer placement policy + DMA ping-pong (services/storage/psram_pool): protocore_psram_place picks
DRAM vs PSRAM by size / DMA requirement / free-heap headroom (large-cold to PSRAM, small-hot + DMA to
DRAM, leaving a DRAM reserve), plus the SPI DMA ping-pong double-buffer index bookkeeping. Pure host tests.

native_ptp_wire.desc: PTPv2 message codec and slave clock math (network_drivers/application/ptp). IEEE 1588-2008 is paywalled, so the field layout is anchored on the IEEE 802.1 working group's published IEEE P802.1AS-Rev/D8.0 text, which carries the PTP common header verbatim: clause 10.6.2 Table 10-7 (octet counts and offsets, 34-octet header), 10.6.2.2.5 (messageLength), 11.4.2.5 (correctionField in nanoseconds scaled by 2^16, with its worked 2.5 ns = 0x0000000000028000 example), Table 10-11 (Announce body), and Tables 11-5 / 11-12 / 11-13 / 11-14 (messageType numbers and the peer-delay message bodies). The 10-octet timestamp is anchored on RFC 8877 sec 4.3, the UDP ports on the IANA port registry, and the offset / mean-path-delay / meanLinkDelay arithmetic is derived from the mechanisms' definitions with the algebra written into the suite.

native_qpack_rfc.desc: QPACK field-section compression (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3/qpack, RFC 9204): the Appendix B.1 worked example decoded octet for octet, the sec 4.5.1 field-section prefix, the sec 4.5.2 / 4.5.4 / 4.5.6 representations and the Appendix A static-table entries they name, a whole field section round trip, refusal of every dynamic-table reference (T=0, post-base, non-zero Required Insert Count), an out-of-range static index, truncation, the scratch bound, an emit refusal, and short-destination refusals.

native_quic_conn.desc:
QUIC v1 server connection engine (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3/quic_conn, RFC 9000
/ RFC 9001): the test acts as a QUIC client - builds real Initial / Handshake / 1-RTT packets and
drives a server QuicConn through a full handshake (per-level AEAD, CRYPTO reassembly, ACKs,
coalescing, HANDSHAKE_DONE) and a 1-RTT request/response stream exchange.

native_quic_crypto_rfc.desc: QUIC packet protection (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3/quic_crypto, RFC 9001 sec 5): the FIPS 197 Appendix C.1 AES-128 block, GCM Test Case 4, the sec 5.2 Initial salt and every secret RFC 9001 Appendix A.1 publishes, the A.3 server Initial protected and unprotected octet for octet, the A.2 client Initial protected header and header-protection sample, the A.4 Retry integrity tag, tamper rejection over header / ciphertext / tag, the parameter bounds, and a 1-RTT short-header round trip whose first-octet mask is five bits rather than four.

native_quic_frame_rfc.desc: QUIC frame coding (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3/quic_frame, RFC 9000 sec 19): the Table 3 type assignments, the single-octet PADDING / PING / HANDSHAKE_DONE frames, the sec 19.3 ACK field order with its ranges and ECN counts, the sec 19.6 CRYPTO frame whose data aliases the packet buffer, the sec 19.8 STREAM type bits OFF/LEN/FIN including the absent-Length case that runs to the end of the packet, MAX_DATA, both CONNECTION_CLOSE variants and the Frame Type field only the transport one carries, the sec 20.1 error codes, the unhandled frames walked past by their wire shape per sec 12.4, and the truncation and short-destination refusals.

native_quic_packet_rfc.desc: QUIC packet headers and packet-number coding (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3/quic_packet, RFC 9000 sec 17): the client Initial, server Initial, Retry and short headers RFC 9001 Appendix A prints as hex, parsed field by field and two of them rebuilt; the Table 5 long packet types; the Fixed Bit requirement; the sec 17.2.1 Version Negotiation packet; the connection-ID and packet-number-length bounds; and the packet-number encode/decode worked examples of RFC 9000 Appendix A.2 and A.3.

native_quic_server.desc:
HTTP/3 server glue (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3/quic_server): the UDP-facing pool
that routes datagrams by Destination Connection ID to a pool of QuicConn + H3Conn engines. A QUIC
client in the test hands datagrams to the pcb the server bound and reads its replies back out of the
host stack's send log, driving a full handshake + HTTP/3 GET and verifying the 200 + body - the same
end-to-end flow as test_h3_e2e but through protocore_quic_server_begin / poll / respond over the real UDP
listener, exercising the connection-ID routing, the ingest ring, and new-connection creation from a
client Initial. The HTTP/3 dispatch bridge (h3_server.c) belongs to native_h3_server: it reaches the
route table and the TCP slot pools, which this env does not build.

native_quic_tls_rfc.desc: The TLS 1.3 server handshake state machine QUIC runs (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3/quic_tls, RFC 9001 / RFC 8446): a full interop round trip in which the test runs the client half - its own X25519, transcript hash and RFC 8446 sec 7.1 key schedule - and requires the Handshake and 1-RTT packet keys to equal the server's, verifies the server Finished, and makes the server accept a client Finished the test computed; the sec 4.4 server flight ordering and the sec 4.1.3 ServerHello fields; the RFC 9001 sec 8.2 transport-parameter extension; and the negotiation refusals with the sec 6.2 alert each one carries.

native_quic_tls_pqc.desc:
TLS 1.3 QUIC handshake with the X25519MLKEM768 post-quantum hybrid group (IANA 0x11ec,
PROTOCORE_ENABLE_PQC_KEX=1): drives the server with a hybrid ClientHello, then verifies it as a conforming
client - ML-KEM Decaps (an independent reference) + X25519, the 64-byte ML-KEM||X25519 secret, and
both Finished MACs. Reuses the classical test_quic_tls suite plus the added hybrid round-trip.

native_quic_tp.desc:
QUIC transport parameters codec (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3/quic_tp, RFC 9000
sec 18): the sec 18.2 defaults, an encode/parse round-trip over the connection IDs + every varint
parameter + the migration flag, parsing a hand-built byte string, skipping unknown/GREASE ids, and
rejecting a duplicate parameter, an oversized connection ID, and out-of-range values.

native_quic_varint.desc:
QUIC variable-length integer codec (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3/quic_varint,
RFC 9000 sec 16) - the foundational HTTP/3 primitive: the Appendix A.1 worked examples (1/2/4/8
byte encodings), the non-minimal decode, length computation, and overflow / truncation guards.

native_radio_power.desc:
WiFi radio power controls (network_drivers/physical/radio_power): modem-sleep mode names
host-tested; the apply/readback are ESP32-only (esp_wifi).

native_radio_sniff_tap.desc: Receive-only radio sniffer pcap framing (services/radio/radio_sniff/radio_sniff.c): the IEEE-754 binary32 encoding of an integer dBm RSSI derived from the format definition, and the IEEE 802.15.4 TAP pseudo-header of that specification's sections 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 3.2 and 3.4 wrapped in a libpcap record with LINKTYPE_IEEE802_15_4_TAP 283. Pure host tests.

native_range.desc:
HTTP Range requests / 206 Partial Content (RFC 7233): full server built with
PROTOCORE_ENABLE_RANGE=1, serving a real littlefs volume through the mount seam and
reading the responses back off the tcp_write capture.

native_rawl2.desc: Raw Layer-2 Ethernet frame codec (services/fieldbus/rawl2): the Ethernet II and 802.1Q VLAN-tagged builders, the parser that separates the two framings, the TCI field widths, and the IEEE 802.3 frame check sequence. Ethertypes checked against the IEEE Registration Authority public EtherType listing; the FCS against the published CRC-32/ISO-HDLC check value 0xCBF43926. Pure host tests.

native_rawmemcpy.desc:
The raw load (mmgr/rawmemcpy.h): bytes at a pointer read as a wider type in the
machine's own order, and the ladder proto_raw_read steps down. Every scalar rung is diffed
against a byte loop written in the test at every offset within a word, so the machine order is
asserted from a runtime endianness probe rather than from a config macro. PROTO_RAW_WORD is
checked against PROTO_WORD_BITS, which the die states, and not against the build machine's
pointer width. The mover is run over the cross product of every destination offset, every source
offset and lengths through two full words: the head loop aligns the destination, so the source
offset is what selects the co-aligned branch or the funnel that joins two adjacent aligned source
words with a shift pair. Poison outside the moved span is checked on every case, so a rung that
writes past its width fails here rather than in the caller that borrowed the next bytes.

native_rcwl0516.desc:
RCWL-0516 Doppler presence sensor + the shared one-GPIO presence facade
(server/peripherals/rcwl0516): the debounce that swallows comparator chatter, the hold that bridges the
module's ~2s retrigger gaps into one continuous presence span, the consume-once edge event,
wrap-safety across a millis() rollover, and the degenerate zero-debounce / zero-hold configs.
Pure core driven by a synthetic clock - no GPIO, no real time. Pure host tests.

native_redis_resp.desc: RESP codec (services/iot/redis_resp), Redis serialization protocol specification: the published LLEN mylist command encoding, and one parse per printed example of Simple strings, Simple errors, Integers, Bulk strings (empty, null and binary-safe), Arrays (empty, nested, null and with null elements), Nulls, Booleans, Doubles (including inf/-inf/nan and exponents), Big numbers, Bulk errors, Verbatim strings, Maps (2 children per entry), Sets and Pushes, plus the refusal of the Attributes type and of any other first byte, the wait-for-the-whole-value framing and the fail-closed encoder. Pure host tests.

native_relay.desc:
TCP relay / DNAT byte pump (server/net/relay): the bidirectional relay engine that
publishes an internal host:port through the server. Tests cover a bidirectional transfer, the
backpressure carry (a send that accepts partial writes), independent half-close with shutdown
propagation, a large multi-step transfer (byte-exact), and a seam error - driven by two mock
sockets over the send/recv seams. Pure host tests.

native_relay_listener.desc: Relay / DNAT listener bind table (server/net/relay/relay_listener): the published front-port binds, the bridge allocator, and the host-length and table-full refusals. The suite includes relay_listener.c so its file-static bind lookup and bridge allocator are reachable, which is why the env does not build that .c itself.

native_response_headers.desc:
test_response_headers against the native_stack_http stack. Carries PROTOCORE_ENABLE_NTP because the
Date-header cases drive the clock through the NTP client's own entry points, and with it the UDP
listener the portable client binds its reply port on.

native_rfc1951.desc: The RFC 1951 sec 3.2.5 length and distance tables and the sec 3.2.6 fixed-Huffman construction over them, defined once in codec/deflate/rfc1951.c and read by both DEFLATE codecs and both SSH zlib codecs. Every expected value is transcribed from RFC 1951, so the tables are checked against the standard rather than against themselves.

native_codec_rfc1951.desc: The RFC 1951 code tables (network_drivers/presentation/codec/deflate/rfc1951): the sec 3.2.5 length and distance tables transcribed from the RFC's own printed rows rather than from the implementation, checked entry by entry and then checked to tile their ranges without a gap all the way to the largest distance of 32768. The sec 3.2.6 fixed-Huffman construction is checked against the four code length runs and against every boundary code that section prints in full, stored bit-reversed because sec 3.1.1 puts a code on the wire most significant bit first while the bit writer packs LSB-first. The two emitters are then driven through a real bit writer and their octets derived by hand: one literal, a shortest back-reference, the single length code for 258, a length whose offset lands in the extra bits, and a writer with no room latching overflow instead of writing past it.

native_ring.desc:
The shared ring primitive (mmgr/ring.h) and its three views: bytes by head/tail, whole
messages by segment, and claimable slots by mask. Both TCP transports and both UDP rings sit on
this file and it had no suite of its own - it was only ever exercised as a side effect of theirs,
which is how the wrap could move from a modulo to a mask on the strength of transport envs alone.
Covers the power-of-two capacity the mask index requires, a wrapped entry reading back whole, a
segment staying invisible until it is published and refusing rather than overwriting one in
flight, and the slot view: first taker wins, ready is marked minus held, next is the lowest set,
and a losing hold cannot redirect the wire by clobbering the winner's keepout.

native_roaming.desc:
Wi-Fi roaming decision layer (network_drivers/network/roaming): the pure policy that fuses the current RSSI, a
candidate neighbour list, and an optional 802.11v BTM hint into a roam/stay decision (target BSSID +
channel + reason), with a hysteresis margin and a disassoc-imminent override. Pure host tests.

native_robotics.desc:
OPC UA for Robotics (OPC 40010-1) MotionDeviceSystem model (services/machine_tool/robotics) - the Browse
hierarchy + the Read resolver over a bound RoboticsMotionDeviceSystem, including the parametric
Axes, are host-tested here. Requires the OPC UA codec. No heap, no stdlib.

native_rtc.desc:
DS1307/DS3231 RTC conversions (server/peripherals/rtc): BCD time registers <-> Unix epoch in
24- and 12-hour encodings, leap years, clock-halt/century bit masks, range validation,
and a round-trip over the 2000-2099 range. Pure - the I2C read/write is ESP32-only.

native_gnss_rtcm3.desc: RTCM 3 framing + station-reference codec (services/timing_position/gnss/rtcm3): the CRC-24Q residue-is-zero identity that pins polynomial, seed, bit order and final XOR at once, the CRC's GF(2) linearity, the 0xD3 / six reserved bits / 10-bit length frame header, parse round trip with need-more and bad-CRC reporting, preamble sync, MSB-first bit I/O with two's-complement signed fields, and the published 1005 (152-bit) and 1006 (168-bit) DF field offsets with the 38-bit ECEF range.

native_s7comm.desc: Siemens S7comm PDU codec (services/fieldbus/s7comm): the Setup Communication / Read Var / Write Var job builders with their 12-octet S7-ANY item specs, the header parser (protocol id, ROSCTR, the 10- vs 12-octet header, the declared lengths), and the response data-item walk with the bit/byte length rule and the even-item padding. Constants and both length rules taken from the Wireshark dissector epan/dissectors/packet-s7comm.c, the reference the module itself cites. Pure host tests.

native_safety_scl.desc:
IEC 61784-3 black-channel Safety Communication Layer primitives (services/machine_tool/safety_scl):
the monitoring-counter state machine, the receive watchdog, and the fail-safe latch the four safety
profiles compose. Covers each way a black channel misbehaves - corruption, loss, duplication,
reordering, insertion - plus the watchdog (incl. a millis() rollover and the disabled case), the
no-silent-reheal latch, counter wrapping at a narrow modulus, and the explicit re-establish. The
CRC is the profile's, not this module's. Pure core on a synthetic clock. Pure host tests.

native_sb_modbus.desc:
Modbus-master southbound driver adapter (services/southbound/sb_modbus): binds the
transport-agnostic Modbus TCP master codec into the southbound driver framework, so an app
reads/writes register points by driver name through the one facade. Host-tested end to end
against the real slave codec (protocore_modbus_process_adu) over a mock transaction seam.

native_scp.desc:
SCP (RCP) protocol wire codec (network_drivers/session/scp): parse an `scp -t/-f <path>` exec command into its
sink/source role + target, parse + build the `C<mode> <size> <name>` control line (octal mode, decimal
size, name; malformed lines rejected), and the ack byte constants. Pure host tests.

native_scp_wire.desc: SCP (rcp) wire codec (network_drivers/session/scp): the exec-command role parse (-t sink, -f source, bundled flags, the target path) and the C<mode> <size> <name> control line, built and parsed. The rcp line protocol has no published specification, so except for the mode field the suite states its expectations as properties (round-trip identity, refusals, boundaries) rather than as conformance. The mode field is a POSIX.1 permission word in octal, and those bit values are derived by hand in the suite.

native_scp_server.desc: The SCP server (session/scp/ssh_scp.c): the rcp SINK state machine over an exec "scp -t <path>" channel - ready ack, C<mode> <size> <name> control line, streamed data, end-of-record byte, final ack. The rcp protocol has no specification; the oracle is OpenSSH's observed control flow, stated as such in the suite. Nothing else in the matrix compiles this file.

native_scpi.desc:
SCPI / IEEE 488.2 instrument-control codec (services/instrumentation/scpi): the command builder
(:-hierarchy header + params + terminator), the response parsers (numeric NR1/NR2/NR3,
boolean, quoted string, definite/indefinite arbitrary block), the STB/ESR/ESE/SRE +
error-queue status model, and the SCPI short/long-form header matcher. Pure host tests.

native_sdi12.desc:
SDI-12 sensor-bus codec (server/peripherals/sdi12): the command builders, the measurement
response parser (atttn), the data-value splitter, and the SDI-12 CRC (compute/encode/verify).
Pure host tests.

native_secure_pool.desc:
The secure pool accessor (mmgr/secure): the SAME pool mechanism as the plaintext side
(mmgr/arena) instantiated a second time at a disjoint address, so only what differs is
covered here - the access and control layer. Reclaiming WIPES, and wipes before the bytes become
available again, so a secret cannot survive its borrow or reach the next tenant; the scope guard
makes that hold on the early-return paths a hand-written wipe gets forgotten on. And the two
pools being disjoint regions means ownership is decided by address alone - a secure pointer can
never be accepted where a plaintext one is required, or the reverse, with no per-allocation
metadata. Allocator mechanics themselves belong to test_arena.

native_sen0192.desc:
SEN0192 microwave motion sensor presence state machine (server/peripherals/sen0192): presence
asserts on an active sample and holds for the configured window after the last active sample, clears
after it, counts clear->present edges, and honors OUT polarity. Pure - the GPIO read is ESP32-only.

native_senml_pack.desc: SenML Pack builders and Record resolver (services/iot/senml), RFC 8428: the sec 5.1.1 and sec 5.1.2 JSON Packs reproduced character for character, the sec 4.2 value fields in their sec 5 JSON types, the sec 6 Table 4 CBOR integer map keys as RFC 8949 encodes them (-2 as 0x21, -3 as 0x22, the rest as themselves) with an integral Number as an integer and a non-integral one as a binary32 float, and the sec 4.6 resolve folding Base Name and Base Time forward, plus the zero-byte reports on a short buffer. Pure host tests.

native_sep2.desc:
IEEE 2030.5 (SEP 2.0) resource codec (services/energy/sep2): the DeviceCapability, EndDevice,
and DERControl XML documents (urn:ieee:std:2030.5:ns), XML-escaped. Pure host tests.

native_sercos.desc: SERCOS III telegram + IDN codec (services/fieldbus/sercos): the IDN encode/decode over its published 16-bit layout (bit 15 S/P, bits 14..12 parameter set, bits 11..0 data block number) exhaustively round-tripped, and the MDT/AT telegram build/parse. The IDN structure is the Sercos / IEC 61800-7-204 addressing scheme; the reduced telegram header layout could not be sourced, so those cases assert properties only. Pure host tests.

native_sftp_server.desc: The SFTP v3 server subsystem (application/sftp/ssh_sftp.c) driven over a real SSH session channel: a subsystem "sftp" CHANNEL_REQUEST tags the channel, SSH_FXP_* requests arrive as CHANNEL_DATA, and responses are read back off the wire. Storage is the RAM mount backend. Expected values are transcribed from draft-ietf-secsh-filexfer-02, the authoritative text for SFTP v3. Nothing else in the matrix compiles this file.

native_sht3x.desc:
Sensirion SHT3x temperature/humidity codec (server/peripherals/sht3x): the CRC-8 against the
datasheet check value (0xBEEF -> 0x92), the raw-tick -> milli-unit temperature/humidity
conversions at the range endpoints and a mid value, and the six-byte single-shot response
parse (both CRCs checked, corrupt CRC rejected). Pure - the I2C transfer is ESP32-only.

native_sigfox_at.desc: Sigfox modem AT-command codec (services/radio/sigfox/sigfox.c): the AT$SF uplink command checked against the published AT$SF=496F54456173746572456767 example, uppercase most-significant-nibble-first hex, the 12-octet Sigfox uplink payload cap, output bounds, and the OK / ERROR / pending classification of a modem reply. Pure host tests.

native_signaling.desc:
Application-layer signaling (server/signaling): the state bucket. Deposits go in from the loop
(response class tallies, and the uptime + conn/listener bitmasks a tick already has in hand), a
read hands back a copy rather than a window, and kill forwards a slot to the transport unchanged.
The module holds no logic by design, so the tests assert exactly that. protocore_conn_close is stubbed:
the forward is what is under test, not lwIP.

native_simatic.desc:
Siemens SIMATIC serial (services/fieldbus/simatic): 3964R block framing (DLE-double + XOR BCC)
+ the 3964R link state machine (STX/DLE handshake, NAK/QVZ retry, ZVZ timeout, priority
arbitration) + RK512 SEND/FETCH/reaction telegram build/parse (big-endian words). Pure host tests.

native_sleep_sched.desc:
Dynamic sleep-cycle scheduler (server/sleep_sched): the wrap-safe idle->sleep-window
decision core with a doubling ramp clamped to a ceiling. Pure host tests, synthetic clock.

native_smb.desc:
SMB2 client (network_drivers/application/smb, MS-SMB2 / MS-NLMP): the SMB2 wire codec (transport frame,
sync header, NEGOTIATE, SESSION_SETUP, TREE_CONNECT/CREATE/CLOSE/READ/WRITE); the NTLM digests
MD4 (RFC 1320) / MD5 (RFC 1321) / HMAC-MD5 (RFC 2104) KAT-verified vs the RFC vectors; the
NTLMv2 response (NThash / NTOWFv2 / NTProofStr / SessionBaseKey) vs the MS-NLMP section 4.2
worked example; the NTLMSSP message codec; the SPNEGO GSS-API DER wrapping (RFC 4178) verified
byte-exact + independently vs openssl; and the smb_client dialogue engine (the full NEGOTIATE
-> NTLMv2 SESSION_SETUP -> TREE_CONNECT -> CREATE -> CLOSE handshake) driven by a scripted mock
SMB2 server over a send/recv seam. Pure host tests.

native_md_kat.desc: MD4, MD5 and HMAC-MD5 (crypto/hash/md.h), the legacy digests NTLM needs. Runs the published test suites whole: RFC 1321 Appendix A.5 for MD5, RFC 1320 Appendix A.5 for MD4, and all seven RFC 2202 section 2 HMAC-MD5 cases including the two with an 80-octet key that RFC 2104 requires be hashed down first. Adds streaming / one-shot agreement at every split, context reuse across the two algorithms, and the 55/56 and 63/64 padding boundaries.

native_ntlm_v2.desc: NTLMv2 response computation (network_drivers/application/smb/ntlm, MS-NLMP). Every expected value comes from MS-NLMP section 4.2 Cryptographic Values for Validation: 4.2.2.1.2 NTOWFv1 (the NT hash of the password), 4.2.4.1.1 NTOWFv2, 4.2.4.1.2 SessionBaseKey, 4.2.4.2.2 the 84-octet NtChallengeResponse and 4.2.4.3's AUTHENTICATE_MESSAGE which carries it. The MsvAvFlags MIC bit follows MS-NLMP 2.2.2.10, and the AUTHENTICATE MIC of 3.1.5.1.2 is checked against the published RFC 2202 HMAC-MD5 test vectors, which also proves the streamed concatenation.

native_ntlmssp.desc: NTLMSSP message codec (network_drivers/application/smb/ntlmssp, MS-NLMP 2.2.1). The CHALLENGE_MESSAGE of MS-NLMP 4.2.4.3 is transcribed from its published hex dump and parsed: the 2.2.1.2 field offsets, the server challenge, and the AV_PAIR blob the NTLMv2 response is computed over. The NEGOTIATE (2.2.1.1) and AUTHENTICATE (2.2.1.3) builders are checked against 4.2.1's identity values in UTF-16LE, with each Len / MaxLen / BufferOffset triplet required to locate its own payload, plus the Version and MIC fields a MIC-carrying AUTHENTICATE reserves (3.1.5.1.2) and the 2.2.2.5 NegotiateFlags bit values.

native_spnego.desc: SPNEGO DER wrapping of the NTLMSSP tokens (network_drivers/application/smb/spnego). Checks the RFC 2743 sec 3.1 InitialContextToken framing and the RFC 4178 sec 4.2.1 NegTokenInit of the first SESSION_SETUP buffer octet for octet, the bare RFC 4178 sec 4.2.2 NegTokenResp of the second, the responseToken walk past negState and supportedMech, the X.690 clause 8.1.3 short and long definite length forms at each nesting level, and fail-closed refusal of indefinite lengths, wrong tags and lengths that run past the buffer. Both OIDs are derived by hand from X.690 clause 8.19.

native_smb2_wire.desc: SMB2 client wire codec (network_drivers/application/smb/smb2, MS-SMB2). Checks the sec 2.2.1.2 SYNC header offset by offset (ProtocolId 0x424D53FE, StructureSize 64, and every field through the 16-octet Signature), its ProtocolId / StructureSize validation, the sec 2.1 Direct TCP 4-octet transport prefix, the sec 2.2.3 NEGOTIATE request body and sec 2.2.4 response parse with a bounds-checked security buffer, the sec 3.1.4.1 / 3.1.5.1 HMAC-SHA256 and AES-CMAC signing round trip with tamper detection, the sec 2.2.41 TRANSFORM_HEADER and sec 3.1.4.3 nonce lengths, an encrypt/decrypt round trip for all four SMB 3.1.1 ciphers with AAD and tag tampering, and the sec 3.1.4.2 key-derivation label separation.

native_smb_pentest.desc: Adversarial harness for the SMB-family parsers that consume untrusted bytes (network_drivers/application/smb: smb2, ntlmssp, spnego) and the bounded string core under them (mmgr/protostr). No standard states what a parser must do with garbage, so the expectations here are stated as properties: fail-closed refusal, a fixed footprint checked with canaries past every destination, and termination whatever the length fields claim. Inputs are deterministic - a fixed-seed xorshift PRNG plus structure-aware mutation of valid messages - so a failure reproduces exactly. Covers length/offset fields walked across their whole range, single-octet mutation of a valid CHALLENGE, truncation at every length, hostile nested DER, builder capacity sweeps, signature verification against every single-bit mutation, and AEAD blobs that must never yield plaintext.

native_smbus.desc:
SMBus 3.1 Packet Error Code (server/peripherals/smbus): the address byte with its direction
bit, the PEC over a write transaction and over a read transaction (which spans both halves and
the repeated-start address), and that the checksum depends on the address and the direction as
well as the payload. The PEC comes from the shared CRC engine, so each vector is checked against
pc_crc(&PROTOCORE_CRC8_SMBUS) directly rather than against a second implementation.

native_smtp.desc:
SMTP client (RFC 5321) dialogue engine (services/net/smtp/smtp_run): greeting/EHLO/AUTH
LOGIN/MAIL/RCPT/DATA over a send/recv seam, with dot-stuffing + multi-line reply
parsing. Driven by a scripted mock server on the host - no lwIP or TLS.

native_snmp.desc:
SNMP ASN.1 BER codec (the version-agnostic base for the SNMP agent). Pure
codec - no lwIP/UDP - so it unit-tests on the host.

native_snmp_ber_x690.desc: SNMP ASN.1 BER codec (services/net/snmp/snmp_ber.c) against ITU-T X.690 clause 8.1 identifier and length octets, 8.3 INTEGER minimal two's complement, 8.7 OCTET STRING, 8.8 NULL and 8.19 OBJECT IDENTIFIER base-128 subidentifiers, plus RFC 3417 section 8 item 1 (definite form only, indefinite prohibited, an over-long definite length permitted) and the RFC 2578 section 7.1.5 through 7.1.8 application-wide type tags. Pure codec over caller buffers, no transport.

native_snmp_notify.desc: SNMP notification originator (services/net/snmp/snmp_notify.c): the SNMPv2-Trap-PDU and InformRequest-PDU of RFC 3416 section 4.2.6 and 4.2.7 with their two mandatory first variable bindings sysUpTime.0 and snmpTrapOID.0 (RFC 3418 section 2), the context-specific PDU tags of RFC 3416 section 3, the RFC 1901 section 3 SNMPv2c message wrapper, and the RFC 2578 section 7.1 value tags each binding type carries. Build calls only - this build has no UDP transport.

native_snmp_v3.desc:
SNMPv3 USM layer: auth (HMAC-SHA-256), privacy (AES-128-CFB), engine discovery,
timeliness. Pulls in the SHA-256/HMAC primitives from the SSH crypto layer.

native_snp.desc:
GE Fanuc SNP serial frame codec (services/fieldbus/snp): the Series Ninety Protocol frame
([control][length][data][BCC]) build + validate, the BCC being the Block Check Code of GE Fanuc
GFK-0582D p. 7-62 (seed zero; per byte, XOR then rotate the accumulator left one bit),
checked against the three X-Attach messages that manual prints with their computed
BCC octets. Pure host tests.

native_sockpool.desc:
Dynamic socket recycling (server/net/sockpool): a fixed LRU connection-slot pool - acquire
(free slot, else recycle the least-recently-used and report the evicted id), touch, release, find, and
in-use count. Pure host tests.

native_southbound.desc:
Southbound protocol-driver framework (services/southbound): the bounded driver registry
(register / find / clear / count) and the name-dispatched read/write/read_block/write_block facade,
including capability + not-found handling and transport-error passthrough. Pure host tests.

native_spa_router.desc:
Single-page-app micro-routing (server/web/spa_router): the serve-file / serve-shell /
passthrough decision from a request path (extension test + API prefix). Pure host tests.

native_span.desc:
The bounded byte region (mmgr/span.h): a pointer and the capacity that belongs to
it, bound together. Rule 19 converts stack arrays - whose length the compiler ties to the object -
into borrowed regions, and the naive rewrite to a bare pointer plus a separate cap argument is
where a 4-byte sizeof() or a mismatched capacity slips through with no diagnostic. Covers the
extent recovered from the array type, the normalization that makes {nullptr, n} unconstructible
so an omitted check writes nothing instead of dereferencing null, and the sub-span clamping that
keeps a truncated frame from producing a pointer past the allocation.

native_sparkplug.desc:
Sparkplug B codec (services/iot/sparkplug): the topic builder + the Metric / Payload
protobuf serializers (over the protobuf codec). Field numbers per the Eclipse Tahu proto.
Pure host tests.

native_storage_sqlite.desc: SQLite3 on-disk file-format reader/writer (services/storage/sqlite): the sec 1.3 database-header offset table, the sec 1.3.2 page-size encoding, the sec 2.1 varint and its 1-9 byte length boundaries, the record serial-type chart, the sec 1.6 b-tree page header and cell pointer array, the sqlite_schema row, sign-extended integer and big-endian IEEE-754 column decoding, whole-table cursor walks and overflow-chain reassembly over real sqlite3-written fixtures, and the bounded writer round-tripped through the reader.

native_ssh.desc: SSH crypto layer (native software paths only, no mbedtls dependency); channels multiplexed (PROTOCORE_SSH_MAX_CHANNELS=3) to exercise routing; SFTP/SCP subsystem routing on (MNT satisfies the guard - the file-transfer servers reach storage through the mount, not through FILE_SERVING)

native_aesgcm_kat.desc: AES-256-GCM (crypto/aead/aesgcm.h) against the NIST CAVP AES-256-GCM known-answer vectors from the SP 800-38D validation set (Keylen 256 / IVlen 96 / Taglen 128): empty message, AAD-only GMAC, one whole block, and a partial final block. Adds tamper refusal on tag, ciphertext, AAD and nonce, the RFC 5647 sec 7.1 invocation-counter advance, the NIST SP 800-38D sec 6.5 GCTR counter byte carry, and in-place sealing.

native_aesgcm_kat_hw.desc: The AES-256-GCM CAVP vectors a second time with the accelerator arm selected, answered by the host AES HAL so both arms run natively.

native_chachapoly_kat.desc: chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com (crypto/aead/chachapoly.h). OpenSSH publishes no vectors for the construction, so the keystream halves are driven onto RFC 8439 Appendix A.1 Test Vectors 1, 2 and 3: an all-zero 64-octet key and sequence number 0 make both ChaCha keys and both nonces all-zero, so the encrypted length field and the encrypted payload must equal the RFC's published counter-0 and counter-1 blocks XORed with the plaintext. A second case gives the two halves different keys so a swapped split cannot pass. The Poly1305 tag is held to properties: verification, tamper refusal on every covered field, and the wrong sequence number.

native_ssh_client.desc: SSH client role (ssh/client/client.c) built per file: nothing else in the matrix compiles it. Covers the tunnel state API, the cfg guard, and the provisioning key derivation, which runs through the connection's compile-time storage.

native_ssh_comp.desc:
SSH s2c compression WIRING with the full SSH stack built with PROTOCORE_ENABLE_SSH_ZLIB=1:
the compression owner (ssh_comp) + its NEWKEYS / USERAUTH_SUCCESS activation + the packet-layer
compress path in ssh_pkt_send. Drives the packet layer directly and reconstructs the continuous
zlib stream from the framed packets, decoding via inflate_raw. Compile-verifies every #if
PROTOCORE_ENABLE_SSH_ZLIB block across transport / server / packet.

native_ssh_conn.desc: SSH wired through the real transport/session layers (PROTO_SSH byte-pump)

native_ssh_ecdsa.desc:
ECDSA P-256 for ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 (RFC 5656) host-tested on the software path: pubkey,
deterministic sign, and verify pinned byte-exact to the RFC 6979 A.2.5 (P-256/SHA-256)
vectors, plus tamper rejection. Self-contained field/point math + RFC 6979 (HMAC-SHA256).

native_ssh_ecdsa_hw.desc: RFC 6979 and RFC 5903 a second time with the accelerated curve backend selected (PROTOCORE_HAS_HW_ECC + the MODMULT field layer), answered by the host RSA/MPI HAL so both arms run natively.

native_curve25519_kat.desc: Curve25519 and Ed25519 (crypto/asymmetric/curve25519.h, ed25519.h): the RFC 7748 sec 5.2 X25519 vectors plus the iterated results after 1 and 1,000 rounds, the RFC 7748 sec 6.1 Diffie-Hellman vector, the sec 5 high-bit mask on a received u-coordinate, and small-order inputs collapsing to zero. Ed25519 is pinned to all four RFC 8032 sec 7.1 vectors (public key and signature), the sec 5.1.7 non-canonical S refusal, and the GF(2^255-19) field identities curve25519.h exports.

native_curve25519_kat_hw.desc: RFC 7748 and RFC 8032 a second time with the MPI accelerator field layer selected (PROTOCORE_FE25519_MPI_HW), answered by the host RSA/MPI HAL so both field arms run natively.

native_rsa_kat.desc: RSASSA-PKCS1-v1.5 over RSA-2048 (crypto/asymmetric/rsa.h) on the software modular multiply. Verify is driven onto Project Wycheproof's rsa_signature_2048_sha256 and _sha512 files at a pinned commit - 97 rows of which 78 are the encoding attacks a lax PKCS#1 parser accepts: BER-encoded padding, altered ASN.1 in the DigestInfo, a missing NULL parameter, short padding, a representative raised past the modulus. Sign is held to signatures openssl produced over a throwaway key whose primes test/vectors/openssl_rsa_2048_sign.json publishes, octet for octet, plus the sign/verify round trip.

native_rsa_kat_hw.desc: RSASSA-PKCS1-v1.5 over RSA-2048 a second time with the accelerated modular multiply selected (PROTOCORE_RSA_MODMUL_HW), answered by the host RSA/MPI HAL so both arms of the multiply run natively against the same vectors.

native_bignum_group14.desc: The 2048-bit big-integer layer (crypto/asymmetric/bignum.h) on the portable software Montgomery backend. group14_p and group14_g are held to RFC 3526 section 3 as printed; the big-endian conversions, the ordering entries, is_zero and the RFC 4253 section 8 DH range check are held to their boundaries; and the group-14 modexp is driven onto nine residues CPython's pow() produced over the same transcribed prime - a small power, Fermat over a prime modulus, a zero exponent, two full-width exponents, and the two halves of an exchange that must land on the same secret.

native_bignum_group14_hw.desc: The same big-integer layer with the accelerated bignum backend selected (PROTOCORE_HAS_HW_BIGNUM), answered by the host arm of the RSA/MPI HAL so both backends of bn_expmod_group14 run natively against the same residues.

native_ssh_flow.desc: The RFC 4254 sec 5.2 channel window (ssh/connection/connection.c): the send cap is the smaller of the peer's window and its maximum packet size, a send decrements the window, an adjust increments it, and the window stops at 2^32-1 because sec 5.2 says it MUST NOT be increased above that. Expected values are transcribed from RFC 4254.

native_ssh_forward.desc: The RFC 4254 sec 7 remote-forward owner (ssh/connection/connection.c, ssh -R). Sec 7.1: tcpip-forward binds a real listener, cancel-tcpip-forward stops it, port 0 is refused rather than allocated, and an SSH connection closing takes its listeners with it; replies follow sec 4 (SUCCESS/FAILURE only when want_reply, bare success, request order). Sec 7.2: a connection arriving on a forwarded port is dispatched through Session.tick and opens a forwarded-tcpip channel whose eight fields are checked against the RFC, then sec 5.1 CHANNEL_OPEN_CONFIRMATION starts the byte bridge and CHANNEL_OPEN_FAILURE drops the socket. Nothing else in the matrix compiles this file.

native_ssh_hardened.desc: SSH built with password auth disabled (publickey-only hardening)

native_ssh_inflate.desc:
SSH client-to-server resumable INFLATE (ssh_inflate): decompresses OpenSSH's per-packet
Z_PARTIAL_FLUSH zlib stream across packets with a 32 KB context-takeover window. Verified against
golden vectors produced by real zlib (windowBits 15, Z_PARTIAL_FLUSH per packet; tools/crypto/gen_ssh_inflate_vectors.py),
covering fixed/dynamic/stored blocks, cross-packet back-references, and empty/tiny payloads. Pure host tests.

native_ssh_kbdint.desc: SSH keyboard-interactive auth (RFC 4256) built with PROTOCORE_ENABLE_SSH_KEYBOARD_INTERACTIVE=1: the server sends one non-echoed Password prompt (INFO_REQUEST) and verifies the INFO_RESPONSE via the password callback. Also re-runs test_ssh_auth to confirm the password/publickey methods are unaffected with keyboard-interactive advertised.

native_ssh_packet.desc: The RFC 4253 sec 6 binary packet protocol (ssh/transport/transport.c): packet_length, the 4..255 padding and its block-size rule, the 16-byte minimum, the sec 6.4 sequence counter, and the SshDir the codec is handed. Expected values are transcribed from RFC 4253, so a failure means the framing drifted from the standard.

native_ssh_pqc.desc:
mlkem768x25519-sha256 SSH hybrid KEX (draft-ietf-sshm-mlkem-hybrid-kex) end to end: the
full SSH transport built with PROTOCORE_ENABLE_PQC_KEX=1 plus the ML-KEM-768 / SHA-3 core. Verifies the
hybrid is negotiated, then runs a real server-side key exchange and checks it as a conforming client
would - ML-KEM Decaps (an independent reference) + X25519, K = SHA256(K_PQ || K_CL), the string-K
exchange hash and KDF, and the ed25519 signature over H.

native_ssh_sftp.desc:
SFTP protocol v3 wire codec (network_drivers/application/sftp): the SSH_FXP_* request reader + response builders
(VERSION / STATUS / HANDLE / DATA / ATTRS / NAME), the ATTRS blob encode/decode round-trip (size / perms /
mtime + the flag word, skipping unknown/extended fields), packet length-framing (need-more vs
malformed/too-big), and the ls -l longname formatter. Pure host tests (no fs / no SSH).

native_sftp_wire.desc: SFTP version 3 wire codec (network_drivers/application/sftp, draft-ietf-secsh-filexfer-02): the sec 3 packet framing whose length field counts the data area and excludes itself, the sec 3 packet type numbers, the sec 5 ATTRS flag bits and field order (including skipping the extended fields), the sec 6.3 SSH_FXP_OPEN pflags, the sec 7 status codes and the STATUS / HANDLE / DATA / NAME / ATTRS response layouts octet by octet, the bounds-checked reader (a string longer than its payload is refused), the length-prefix backfill, and the ls -l longname whose permission column is derived from POSIX.1 permission bits.

native_ssh_zlib.desc:
SSH server-to-client streaming compressor (zlib@openssh.com / zlib): a context-takeover
DEFLATE stream (persistent sliding window across packets, sync-flush per packet, zlib
wrapper). The whole session is one zlib stream, so concatenating packets and decoding via
inflate_raw (validated vs Python zlib in test_inflate) proves cross-packet back-references
resolve; packet-by-packet decodability under a reference zlib.decompressobj (OpenSSH's model)
is cross-checked out-of-tree.

native_stack_http.desc: Full HTTP/1.1 server stack through Layer 7. Base env for the suites that build on it; it runs no suite of its own.

native_stack_l46.desc:
Layers 4-6 stack: transport + session + presentation + the standalone parser, no app layer. Base env for the suites that build on it; it runs no suite of its own.
These suites predate the RFC 7230 §5.4 Host rule and feed bare HTTP/1.1
request lines to exercise parser mechanics; Host enforcement is verified
separately in env:native_compliance.

native_statsd.desc:
StatsD metrics client (services/iot/statsd): the pure line formatter (name:value|type,
sample rate, DogStatsD tags) plus the count/gauge/timing/set emit helpers, whose sent
bytes are captured through the transport UDP service's host seam.

native_stomp.desc:
STOMP 1.2 frame codec (services/iot/stomp): the zero-heap frame builder (command +
escaped headers + NUL body) + the non-mutating parser (command/header slices/body,
honoring content-length) + escape/unescape. Pure host tests.

native_sunspec.desc:
SunSpec Modbus model codec (services/energy/sunspec): the map writer (marker / model
headers / points / end model) + the model-chain walker + typed point readers
(u16 / i16 / u32 / i32 / string). Pure host tests.

native_swar.desc:
Lane math (mmgr/swar.h): one 32-bit word as four byte lanes. has-zero across
every lane, the guard-bit range compares the base64 decoder classifies with, and the bounded
NUL scan diffed against strnlen at every length, NUL position, and alignment.

native_syslog.desc:
Syslog client (RFC 5424) line formatter. Pure formatter - no lwIP/UDP - so it
unit-tests on the host (udp_transport provides host stubs for protocore_udp_sendto).

native_tcp.desc:
The TCP path a stack drives, run on the host against the pcb driver in core_setup/hal/host. This is the only env that compiles the marshaled
arm of tcp_conn.c - every send, output, close, abort and recved the target routes through
pc_tcp_marshal - and the only one that drives a segment through the callbacks listener_accept_cb
installed on the pcb rather than naming lowlevel_recv_cb directly.

native_tcp_client.desc:
tcp_client.h: the outbound client pool - slot claim, the non-blocking resolve/connect
pump, the whole-open timeout bound, the wire ring and its ack-on-consume window
reopening (RFC 9293 sec 3.8.6). PROTOCORE_ENABLE_HTTP_CLIENT turns PROTOCORE_NEED_CLIENT
on, which is what compiles the translation unit's body at all.

native_tcp_conn.desc:
tcp_conn.h: the connection pool, its RX ring and the stack callback seam, against
RFC 9293 sec 3.6 (close drains before release), 3.6.1 (data after close), 3.8.6
(ack-on-consume window management, SHLD-14), 3.10.5 (abort) and 3.10.8 (user timeout).

native_tcp_evt.desc:
tcp_evt.h: the event type and record every layer above the transport reads - the packed
one-byte enum the listener queue storage is sized on, and a round trip through a real
platform queue.

native_tcp_listener.desc:
tcp_listener.h: the accept callback, listener lifecycle, per-listener event queues,
and the accept-time gates. Throttle budgets overridden small so the boundaries are
explicit; allowlist prefix matching per RFC 4632.

native_tcp_ns.desc:
tcp.h: the one exported table joining the three halves, and that every member of each
half binds to the function its name promises - ConnPool's initializer is positional,
so a member inserted in the header would silently shift the bindings.

native_telemetry.desc:
Telemetry math (services/iot/telemetry): moving-window stats, rate-of-change, and
totalizer. Pure computation (synthetic clock passed in), so it unit-tests on
the host.

native_telnet.desc:
Telnet server (RFC 854 IAC negotiation + line editing) wired through the real
transport ring buffer; output checked via the tcp_write capture mock.

native_radio_thread.desc:
Thread spinel / HDLC-lite framing codec (services/radio/thread). The FCS is pinned twice: to the
CRC-16/X-25 catalogue check value 0x906E and to RFC 1662 Appendix C's good-FCS residue 0xf0b8
(complemented to 0x0F47, since X-25 folds the final XOR in), so the receiver-side acceptance test
the RFC specifies is what governs the checksum. RFC 1662 sec 4.2 supplies the byte-stuffing table
verbatim (7E/7D/11/13). The spinel layer covers the packed unsigned integer (the protocol
reference's 1337 -> B9 0A example plus the 7-bit-group boundaries), the FLG/NLI/TID header byte,
command build/parse through HDLC, the typed value cursors with their little-endian wire layout and
bounds latching, and the property + LAST_STATUS registries.

native_time_compat.desc:
Reentrant broken-down UTC (shared/time_compat): the seam over gmtime_r / gmtime_s, that it
fills the caller's struct rather than a shared static, and the C field conventions
(tm_year from 1900, tm_mon and tm_yday from 0, tm_wday from Sunday). Pure host tests.

native_time_fallback.desc: Multi-source time fallback matrix (services/timing_position/time_source): ascending-priority query of the registered time sources, first-nonzero-wins fallback, that nothing below the source that answered is invoked, the bounded BSS table, and reset. The Date seam is anchored on the RFC 9110 sec 5.6.7 IMF-fixdate example (epoch 784111777 -> 'Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 GMT'), so the registry and the shared formatter are proven joined. Pure host tests with mock sources.

native_tls13_kdf.desc:
TLS 1.3 key schedule for the QUIC handshake (network_drivers/tls/tls13_kdf,
RFC 8446 sec 7.1 / 4.4.4): Early/Handshake/Master secret Extract chain, client/server handshake +
application traffic secrets, the server handshake write key/iv label path, and the server Finished
verify_data over a full ClientHello..CertificateVerify transcript. Pinned to RFC 8448 sec 3.

native_tls13_msg.desc:
TLS 1.3 handshake messages for the QUIC handshake (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3/
tls13_msg, RFC 8446 sec 4): ClientHello parse (X25519 key_share + capability flags), and the server
flight. Byte-exact vs RFC 8448 sec 3 for ServerHello / Certificate / Finished, plus the ALPN + QUIC
transport-params EncryptedExtensions and an Ed25519 CertificateVerify sign/verify round-trip.

native_tls_conn.desc:
TLS 1.3 handshake driver over the stream record layer (network_drivers/tls/tls_conn,
RFC 8446 sec 4): the module drives both ends, so the test stands a client and a server up against
each other and runs the full handshake - ClientHello, the server flight, both Finished messages -
then checks the two installed the same application-traffic keys by sealing on one end and opening
on the other. Around that: the profile refusals (a ClientHello without TLS 1.3, without X25519,
without a key_share, without Ed25519, or offering no cipher suite this stack implements) and the
alert each ends on. The message bytes are pinned against RFC 8448 in test_tls13_msg and the key
schedule in test_tls13_kdf; what this adds is the state machine and the one secure-pool borrow it
runs out of.

native_tls_policy.desc:
TLS version negotiation + pinned cipher policy (server/security/tls_policy): the server-style
version pick (highest supported not above the client's), the version name, cipher selection by server
preference from the offered set, and the AEAD-suite classifier. Pure host tests.

native_tls_record.desc:
TLS 1.3 stream record layer (network_drivers/tls/tls_record, RFC 8446 sec 5), the software arm
selected when the vendor ships no TLS stack (PROTOCORE_TLS_SOFTWARE): the 5-byte TLSPlaintext header and
its length-validating parse, TLSCiphertext protect/unprotect with the real content type sealed
inside the record, the iv XOR seq nonce, the backward scan that recovers the type past the padding,
and the record counter that never travels and does not advance on a forged record. The key + record
KAT is byte-exact against an independent reconstruction (tools/crypto/gen_tls_record_kat.py):
stdlib HKDF-Expand-Label under the "tls13 " prefix plus OpenSSL AES-128-GCM. Pure host tests.

native_tls_seam.desc: The slot-indexed TLS surface (network_drivers/tls/tls.c): the RFC 7250 raw-public-key credential, standing a connection up on a slot, the RFC 8446 sec 5.1 record framing out of the slot's receive ring (partial, short-of-header and over-long fragments all consume nothing), a malformed record failing the connection with an alert, a write before the application keys are installed reaching no wire, and a free that wipes every key generation. This surface was eleven ungated stubs returning -1 until 2026-08-18, so it had no coverage at all.

native_security_totp.desc: One-time passwords (services/security/totp): HOTP over HMAC-SHA-1 against the RFC 4226 Appendix D test values (counts 0-9, the 6-digit HOTP column and the published truncated decimals reduced to 8 digits), TOTP against the RFC 6238 Appendix B SHA1 rows cross-checked at the published value of T, the sec 4.2 time-step floor with T0/X, the sec 6 drift window, and the RFC 4648 sec 10 base32 vectors for the provisioning secret.

native_trace_capture.desc:
Pre/post-trigger sample-window assembler (server/signaling/trace_capture), v5 high-rate
acquisition: a continuously-running pre-trigger ring, trigger() freezing it as the window's
pre-trigger half, feed() filling the post-trigger half and firing the sink on completion,
one capture in flight fail-closed (dropped triggers counted), samples fed before begin() /
after end() counted dropped, and multiple sequential windows with a correct trace_id
